bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第195卷卷第一百九十五

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 195, Scroll Number One Hundred Ninety-Five
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 195

sentences.zh: 【唐紀十一】 起強圉作噩五月，盡上章困敦，凡三年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 11] Beginning in the fifth month of the year qiángyù zuò'è, ending in the year shàngzhāng kùndūn, altogether a little more than three years.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 11] From the fifth month of 639 through 642—a span of a little more than three years.

sentences.zh: 五月，壬申，魏徵上疏，以為：「陛下欲善之志不及於昔時，聞過必改少虧於曩日，譴罰積多，威怒微厲。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day ren-shen, Wei Zheng submitted a memorial, stating: "Your Majesty's resolve to pursue goodness no longer matches former times; readiness to reform upon hearing of faults has declined somewhat from days past; reproofs and punishments have accumulated, and majesty and anger have grown slightly severe.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the day ren-shen, Wei Zheng presented a memorial in which he wrote: "Your Majesty's zeal to do good no longer measures up to what it once was; your willingness to correct yourself when faults are reported has fallen somewhat short of earlier days; censures and punishments have piled up, and your tone of imperial sternness and wrath has grown sharper.

sentences.zh: 乃知貴不期驕，富不期侈，非虛言也。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that nobility does not await arrogance, and wealth does not await extravagance—this is no empty saying.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that high rank does not wait to breed arrogance and riches do not wait to breed extravagance—the saying is no idle phrase.

sentences.zh: 且以隋之府庫、倉廩、戶口、甲兵之盛，考之今日，安得擬倫！

translations.literal: Moreover, comparing the abundance of the Sui treasury, granaries, population, and armor and weapons with the present day, how could they be placed on the same level!
translations.idiomatic: When you compare the Sui dynasty's overflowing treasuries, granaries, population, and armaments with our realm today, how can the two even be mentioned in the same breath!

sentences.zh: 然隋以富強動之而危，我以寡弱靜之而安；

translations.literal: Yet the Sui, though rich and strong, stirred itself into danger, while we, though few and weak, kept still and attained security;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Sui, for all its wealth and power, stirred itself into peril, while we, though comparatively few and weak, have kept still and remained secure;

sentences.zh: 安危之理，皎然在目。

translations.literal: the principle of security and danger lies clearly before the eyes.
translations.idiomatic: the lesson of safety and ruin lies plain before our eyes.

sentences.zh: 昔隋之未亂也，自謂必無亂；

translations.literal: Formerly, before the Sui fell into disorder, it believed itself certain not to fall into disorder;
translations.idiomatic: Before the Sui fell into chaos, it was convinced that chaos could never come;

sentences.zh: 其未亡也，自謂必無亡。

translations.literal: before it perished, it believed itself certain not to perish.
translations.idiomatic: before it perished, it was equally convinced that it could never perish.

sentences.zh: 故賦役無窮，征伐不息，以至禍將及身而尚未之寤也。

translations.literal: Therefore levies and corvée were endless and campaigns unceasing, until calamity was about to reach their persons and they had still not awakened to it.
translations.idiomatic: Hence endless levies and corvée, campaigns without cease—until disaster was upon them and they still had not woken to it.

sentences.zh: 夫鑒形莫如止水，鑒敗莫如亡國。

translations.literal: To mirror one's form, nothing is like still water; to mirror defeat, nothing is like a perished state.
translations.idiomatic: Still water is the best mirror for one's face; a fallen kingdom is the best mirror for one's rule.

sentences.zh: 伏願取鑒於隋，去奢從約，親忠遠佞，以當今之無事，行疇昔之恭儉，則盡善盡美，固無得而稱焉。

translations.literal: I humbly wish that Your Majesty take the Sui as a mirror, cast off extravagance and follow restraint, draw near the loyal and keep the sycophantic at a distance, and in this present time of peace practice the reverence and frugality of former days—then perfection in goodness and beauty would indeed be beyond praise.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg Your Majesty to take the Sui as your warning, renounce luxury for simplicity, keep the loyal close and the flatterers far away, and in these peaceful times practice the reverence and frugality of your early reign—then your virtue would be complete beyond any praise one could offer.

sentences.zh: 夫取之實難，守之甚易，陛下能得其所難，豈不能保其所易乎！」

translations.literal: To take the realm is truly difficult; to keep it is very easy. Your Majesty was able to accomplish what is difficult—can you not preserve what is easy!"
translations.idiomatic: Winning the realm was hard; keeping it is easy. Your Majesty mastered what was hard—surely you can guard what is easy!"

sentences.zh: 六月，右僕射虞恭公溫彥博薨。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, the Duke of Reverence Yu Wen Yanbo, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Wen Yanbo, Duke of Reverence and Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, died.

sentences.zh: 彥博久掌機務，知無不為。

translations.literal: Yanbo had long managed state affairs and did whatever he knew should be done.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo had long handled the machinery of government and left nothing undone that he knew ought to be done.

sentences.zh: 上謂侍臣曰：「彥博以憂國之故，精神耗竭，我見其不逮，已二年矣，恨不縱其安逸，竟夭天年！」

translations.literal: The emperor said to his attending officials: "Yanbo, because of concern for the state, exhausted his spirit and strength. I saw that he could not keep up—for two years already. I regret that I did not allow him ease and leisure; in the end he died before his time!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his attendants: "Yanbo wore himself out worrying over the state. I saw him failing—for two years now. I regret that I did not let him rest; in the end he died before his time!"

sentences.zh: 丁巳，上幸明德宮。

translations.literal: On the day ding-si, the emperor visited Mingde Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the day ding-si, the emperor went to Mingde Palace.

sentences.zh: 己未，詔荊州都督荊王元景等二十一王所任刺史，咸令子孫世襲。

translations.literal: On the day ji-wei, an edict declared that the prefects appointed by the twenty-one princes, including Jing Wang Yuanjing, regional commander of Jingzhou, should all be hereditary in their descendants.
translations.idiomatic: On the day ji-wei, an edict ordered that the prefects appointed by the twenty-one princes, including Prince Jing Yuanjing as regional commander of Jingzhou, should pass their posts to their descendants in perpetuity.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，又以功臣長孫無忌等十四人為刺史，亦令世襲，非有大故，無得黜免。

translations.literal: On the day wu-chen, the fourteen meritorious officials including Zhangsun Wuji were also made prefects, likewise to be hereditary; unless there was grave cause, they could not be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wu-chen, fourteen meritorious ministers including Zhangsun Wuji were likewise appointed prefects with hereditary tenure, not to be removed except for grave cause.

sentences.zh: 己巳，徙許王元祥為江王。

translations.literal: On the day ji-si, Prince Xu Yuanxiang was transferred to be Prince Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: On the day ji-si, Prince Xu Yuanxiang was redesignated Prince Jiang.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸未，大雨，穀、洛溢入洛陽宮，壞官寺、民居，溺死者六千餘人。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day gui-wei, heavy rain fell; the Gu and Luo rivers overflowed into Luoyang Palace, destroying government offices and temples and private dwellings; more than six thousand people drowned.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day gui-wei, torrential rains caused the Gu and Luo rivers to flood into Luoyang Palace, destroying government buildings and private homes; more than six thousand people drowned.

sentences.zh: 魏徵上疏，以為：「《文子》曰：『同言而信，信在言前；

translations.literal: Wei Zheng submitted a memorial, stating: "The Wenzi says: 'When words are the same, trust is placed in them; trust lies before the words;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng presented a memorial in which he wrote: "The Wenzi says: 'When the words are the same, people believe them—but belief rests on what came before the words;

sentences.zh: 同令而行，誠在令外。』

translations.literal: when orders are the same, they are carried out; sincerity lies outside the orders.'
translations.idiomatic: when the orders are the same, people obey them—but sincerity rests on what lies outside the orders.'

sentences.zh: 自王道休明，十有餘年，然而德化未洽者，由待下之情未盡誠信故也。

translations.literal: Since the royal way has been splendid and clear for more than ten years, yet moral transformation has not been fully achieved, this is because the feeling with which you treat those below has not been wholly sincere and trustworthy.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years the royal way has been bright, yet moral transformation has not fully taken hold—because the sincerity with which Your Majesty treats those below has not been complete.

sentences.zh: 今立政致治，必委之君子；

translations.literal: Now in establishing government and bringing order, you must entrust affairs to gentlemen;
translations.idiomatic: To establish policy and govern well, you must entrust affairs to gentlemen;

sentences.zh: 事有得失，或訪之小人。

translations.literal: when affairs have gains or losses, you sometimes consult petty men.
translations.idiomatic: yet when something goes right or wrong, you sometimes consult petty men instead.

sentences.zh: 其待君子也敬而疏，遇小人也輕而狎；

translations.literal: You treat gentlemen with respect but keep them at a distance; you meet petty men lightly but intimately;
translations.idiomatic: You treat gentlemen with respect yet keep them at arm's length; you meet petty men casually yet intimately;

sentences.zh: 狎則言無不盡，疏則情不上通。

translations.literal: intimacy means their words are never withheld; distance means their feelings do not reach you.
translations.idiomatic: intimacy means they tell you everything; distance means their true counsel never reaches you.

sentences.zh: 夫中智之人，豈無小慧！

translations.literal: Men of middling intelligence—do they lack small cleverness!
translations.idiomatic: Men of ordinary talent—do they lack petty cleverness!

sentences.zh: 然才非經國，慮不及遠，雖竭力盡誠，猶未免有敗；

translations.literal: Yet their talent is not for governing the state, their foresight does not reach far; though they exhaust their strength and sincerity, they still cannot avoid failure;
translations.idiomatic: Yet their talent is not equal to governing the realm, their vision does not reach far ahead; though they strain every nerve in loyalty, they still cannot avoid disaster;

sentences.zh: 況內懷奸宄，其禍豈不深乎！

translations.literal: how much more when they harbor treachery within—their harm can hardly be shallow!
translations.idiomatic: how much more when they harbor treachery within—can the harm they do be anything but deep!

sentences.zh: 夫雖君子不能無小過，苟不害於正道，斯可略矣。

translations.literal: Although even gentlemen cannot be without small faults, if they do not harm the correct way, these may be overlooked.
translations.idiomatic: Even gentlemen have small faults; if they do not injure the right path, they may be overlooked.

sentences.zh: 既謂之君子而復疑其不信，何異立直木而疑其影之曲乎！

translations.literal: Having called them gentlemen yet doubting their trustworthiness—how is this different from setting up a straight tree and doubting that its shadow is crooked!
translations.idiomatic: To call a man a gentleman and then doubt his loyalty—is that not like planting a straight post and suspecting its shadow of bending!

sentences.zh: 陛下誠能慎選君子，以禮信用之，何憂不治！

translations.literal: If Your Majesty can truly choose gentlemen carefully and employ them with ritual and trust, what worry is there of failing to govern well!
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will choose gentlemen carefully and employ them with courtesy and trust, what need is there to fear that the realm will not be well governed!

sentences.zh: 不然，危亡之期，未可保也。」

translations.literal: Otherwise, the time of peril and ruin cannot be guaranteed away."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, the day of peril and ruin cannot be far off."

sentences.zh: 上賜手詔褒美曰：「昔晉武帝平吳之後，志意驕怠，何曾位極台司，不能直諫，乃私語子孫，自矜明智，此不忠之大者也。

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed an imperial letter in his own hand praising him, saying: "Formerly, after Emperor Wu of Jin pacified Wu, his will grew proud and slack. He Zeng stood at the summit of the bureaucracy yet could not remonstrate directly; he only spoke privately to his descendants, priding himself on wisdom—this was the greatest disloyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied with a personal edict of praise: "After Emperor Wu of Jin pacified Wu, his spirit turned proud and slack. He Zeng stood at the head of the bureaucracy yet could not speak plainly to the throne; he only whispered to his descendants and prided himself on his shrewdness—that was disloyalty of the worst kind.

sentences.zh: 得公之諫，朕知過矣。

translations.literal: Receiving your remonstrance, I know my fault.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to your remonstrance, I know my fault.

sentences.zh: 當置之幾案以比弦、韋。」

translations.literal: I shall place it on my desk to compare with the bowstring and the whetstone."
translations.idiomatic: I shall keep it on my desk as a constant reminder, like the bowstring and the whetstone."

sentences.zh: 乙未，車駕還洛陽，詔：「洛陽宮為水所毀者，少加修繕，才令可居。

translations.literal: On the day yi-wei, the imperial carriage returned to Luoyang. An edict stated: "Where Luoyang Palace was destroyed by water, repair it slightly, only enough to make it habitable.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yi-wei, the emperor returned to Luoyang and issued an edict: "Where Luoyang Palace was damaged by the flood, make only such repairs as are needed for habitation.

sentences.zh: 自外眾材，給城中壞廬舍者。

translations.literal: All other timber and materials shall be given to those whose houses in the city were ruined.
translations.idiomatic: All other building materials shall go to those whose homes in the city were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 令百官各上封事，極言朕過。」

translations.literal: Let all officials each submit sealed memorials, speaking to the utmost of my faults."
translations.idiomatic: Let every official submit a sealed memorial speaking freely of my faults."

sentences.zh: 壬寅，廢明德宮及飛山之玄圃院，給遭水者。

translations.literal: On the day ren-yin, Mingde Palace and the Mystic Garden compound on Mount Fei were abolished and given to those who had suffered from the flood.
translations.idiomatic: On the day ren-yin, Mingde Palace and the Mystic Garden estate on Mount Fei were dismantled and their materials given to flood victims.

sentences.zh: 八月，甲子，上謂侍臣曰：「上封事者皆言朕遊獵太頻；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day jia-zi, the emperor said to his attending officials: "Those who submitted sealed memorials all said that I hunt too frequently;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the day jia-zi, the emperor told his attendants: "Everyone who submitted sealed memorials said I hunt too often;

sentences.zh: 今天下無事，武備不可忘，朕時與左右獵於後苑，無一事煩民，夫亦何傷！」

translations.literal: now that the realm is at peace, military readiness must not be forgotten. I sometimes hunt in the rear park with my attendants; not a single matter troubles the people—what harm is there!"
translations.idiomatic: yet the realm is at peace and military readiness must not be forgotten. I sometimes hunt in the rear park with my attendants without troubling the people in the least—what harm is there in that!"

sentences.zh: 魏徵曰：「先王惟恐不聞其過。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng said: "The former kings feared only that they would not hear of their faults.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng replied: "The sage kings of old feared only that they would not hear of their faults.

sentences.zh: 陛下既使之上封事，止得恣其陳述。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has already had them submit sealed memorials; you can only let them state their views freely.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty invited sealed memorials; you must let men speak their minds freely.

sentences.zh: 苟其言可取，固有益於國；

translations.literal: If their words are acceptable, they will surely benefit the state;
translations.idiomatic: If what they say is sound, it will surely benefit the state;

sentences.zh: 若其無取，亦無所損。」

translations.literal: if they are not acceptable, there is likewise no loss."
translations.idiomatic: if it is not, there is no harm done either."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「公言是也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your words are correct."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "You are right."

sentences.zh: 皆勞而遣之。

translations.literal: All were rewarded and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded them all and sent them away.

sentences.zh: 侍御史馬周上疏，以為：「三代及漢，歷年多者八百，少者不減四百，良以恩結人心，人不能忘故也。

translations.literal: The attendant censor Ma Zhou submitted a memorial, stating: "The Three Dynasties and Han endured as long as eight hundred years and no less than four hundred, truly because kindness bound people's hearts and they could not forget.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Censor Ma Zhou presented a memorial in which he wrote: "The Three Dynasties and the Han lasted as long as eight hundred years and no less than four hundred, because kindness bound the people's hearts and they could not forget.

sentences.zh: 自是以降，多者六十年，少者才二十餘年，皆無恩於人，本根不固故也。

translations.literal: From then on, the longest was sixty years and the shortest only a little more than twenty—all because they showed no kindness to the people and their roots were not firm.
translations.idiomatic: Since then the longest reign has been sixty years and the shortest barely twenty—all because they showed no kindness to the people and their foundations were not firm.

sentences.zh: 陛下當隆禹、湯、文、武之業，為子孫立萬代之基，豈得但持當年而已！

translations.literal: Your Majesty ought to exalt the achievements of Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu and lay a foundation for ten thousand generations for your descendants—how can you be content merely to hold the present year!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should raise high the achievements of Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu and lay a foundation for ten thousand generations—how can you be content merely to hold power for a single reign!

sentences.zh: 今之戶口不及隋之什一，而給役者兄去弟還，道路相繼。

translations.literal: Today's registered population does not reach a tenth of the Sui's, yet those serving corvée go out as elder brothers and return as younger brothers, one after another on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Today's population is less than a tenth of the Sui's, yet men on corvée duty leave as elder brothers and return as younger ones, filing endlessly along the roads.

sentences.zh: 陛下雖加恩詔，使之裁損，然營繕不休，民安得息！

translations.literal: Although Your Majesty has issued gracious edicts ordering reductions, construction and repair never cease—how can the people rest!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has issued gracious edicts ordering cutbacks, yet construction and repair never cease—how can the people find rest!

sentences.zh: 故有司徒行文書，曾無事實。

translations.literal: Hence there are documents from the Minister of Works that have no relation to reality.
translations.idiomatic: Hence memorials from the Minister of Works that bear no relation to what is actually done.

sentences.zh: 昔漢之文、景，恭儉養民，武帝承其豐富之資，故能窮奢極欲而不至於亂。

translations.literal: Formerly, Emperors Wen and Jing of Han were reverent and frugal and nurtured the people; Emperor Wu inherited their abundant resources and therefore could exhaust luxury and desire without falling into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Wen and Jing of Han were reverent and frugal and nurtured the people; Emperor Wu inherited their accumulated wealth and could indulge every luxury without bringing the realm to ruin.

sentences.zh: 向使高祖之後即傳武帝，漢室安得久存乎！

translations.literal: If the line had passed directly from Gaozu to Emperor Wu, how could the house of Han have long endured!
translations.idiomatic: Had the throne passed directly from Gaozu to Emperor Wu, how long could the house of Han have survived!

sentences.zh: 又，京師及四方所造乘輿器用及諸王、妃、主服飾，議者皆不以為儉。

translations.literal: Moreover, the imperial carriages, utensils, and the apparel of princes, consorts, and princesses made in the capital and throughout the realm—commentators all consider them not frugal.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the imperial equipage, furnishings, and the dress of princes, consorts, and princesses made in the capital and the provinces are widely judged not to be frugal.

sentences.zh: 夫昧爽丕顯，後世猶怠，陛下少居民間，知民疾苦，尚復如此，況皇太子生長深宮，不更外事，萬歲之後，固聖慮所當憂也。

translations.literal: Though one rise early and make great display, later generations still grow slack. Your Majesty lived among the people in youth and knows their hardships—yet it is still thus; how much more when the crown prince, reared deep in the palace and unacquainted with outside affairs, succeeds you—this is surely what sagely concern ought to dwell on.
translations.idiomatic: Even when a ruler rises early and shines brightly, later ages grow slack. Your Majesty knew the people's hardships in youth—yet things are already thus; when the crown prince, raised deep in the palace and knowing nothing of the world outside, succeeds you, that is what Your Majesty's far-sighted concern should address.

sentences.zh: 臣觀自古以來，百姓愁怨，聚為盜賊，其國未有不亡者，人主雖欲追改，不能復全。

translations.literal: I observe that from antiquity onward, when the people groan in resentment and gather as bandits, their states have never failed to perish; though the ruler may wish afterward to amend matters, he cannot make things whole again.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout history, when the people groan in resentment and gather as bandits, their states have never failed to fall; though a ruler may wish to mend matters afterward, he cannot make the realm whole again.

sentences.zh: 故當修於可修之時，不可悔之於既失之後也。

translations.literal: Therefore one must reform while reform is still possible; one cannot repent only after what is lost is already lost.
translations.idiomatic: Reform must come while reform is still possible—not repentance only after all is already lost.

sentences.zh: 蓋幽、厲嘗笑桀、紂矣，煬帝亦笑周、齊矣，不可使後之笑今如今之笑煬帝也！

translations.literal: King You and King Li once laughed at Jie and Zhou; Emperor Yang also laughed at the Zhou of the Northern Qi—let not posterity laugh at the present as the present laughs at Emperor Yang!
translations.idiomatic: King You and King Li once mocked Jie and Zhou; Emperor Yang mocked the Zhou and Qi dynasties in turn—do not let posterity mock our age as we mock Emperor Yang!

sentences.zh: 貞觀之初，天下饑歉，斗米直匹絹，而百姓不怨者，知陛下憂念不忘故也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, the realm suffered famine; a dou of grain cost a bolt of silk, yet the people did not resent it because they knew Your Majesty's anxious concern had not been forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhenguan era the realm was famine-stricken—a dou of grain cost a bolt of silk—yet the people did not complain because they knew Your Majesty had not forgotten their plight.

sentences.zh: 今比年豐穰，匹絹得粟十餘斛，而百姓怨咨者，知陛下不復念之，多營不急之務故也。

translations.literal: Now, year after year, harvests are abundant; a bolt of silk buys more than ten hu of grain, yet the people complain because they know Your Majesty no longer thinks of them and undertakes many tasks that are not urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Now harvests have been abundant for years—a bolt of silk buys more than ten hu of grain—yet the people grumble because they know Your Majesty no longer cares for them and pursues many undertakings that are not urgent.

sentences.zh: 自古以來，國之興亡，不以畜積多少，在於百姓苦樂。

translations.literal: From antiquity onward, the rise and fall of states has not depended on how much was stored up, but on whether the people suffered or rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity onward, whether a state rose or fell has never depended on how much it hoarded, but on whether the people suffered or prospered.

sentences.zh: 且以近事驗之，隋貯洛口倉而李密因之，東都積布帛而世充資之，西京府庫亦為國家之用，至今未盡。

translations.literal: Test this by recent events: the Sui stored grain at the Luokou granary and Li Mi drew on it; the Eastern Capital amassed cloth and silk and Shi Miangu supplied himself from it; the Western Capital treasuries likewise served the state's use and are not yet exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Recent events prove it: the Sui filled the Luokou granary and Li Mi drew on it; the Eastern Capital hoarded cloth and silk and Wang Shichong armed himself from it; the Western Capital treasuries likewise supplied our state and are not yet exhausted.

sentences.zh: 夫畜積固不可無，要當人有餘力，然後收之，不可強斂以資寇敵也。

translations.literal: Storage is indeed indispensable, but one must collect only when the people have surplus strength; one must not levy by force to supply enemy bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Hoarding is necessary, but only when the people have surplus strength to give; forced levies only stock the arsenals of rebels.

sentences.zh: 夫儉以息人，陛下已於貞觀之初親所履行，在於今日為之，固不難也。

translations.literal: Frugality to give the people rest—Your Majesty personally practiced this at the beginning of Zhenguan; to do so today would surely not be difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Frugality to give the people rest—Your Majesty practiced this yourself at the start of Zhenguan; to do so again today would not be hard.

sentences.zh: 陛下必欲為久長之謀，不必遠求上古，但如貞觀之初，則天下幸甚。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly wishes to plan for long endurance, you need not seek far-off antiquity—only be as at the beginning of Zhenguan, and the realm would be greatly blessed.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly wishes to plan for the long term, you need not look to remote antiquity—only return to the ways of early Zhenguan, and the realm would be blessed indeed.

sentences.zh: 陛下寵遇諸王，頗有過厚者，萬代之後，不可不深思也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's favor toward the princes has in some cases been rather excessive; for ten thousand generations hence, this cannot but be pondered deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has favored some of the princes excessively; for generations to come, this demands deep thought.

sentences.zh: 且魏武帝愛陳思王，及文帝即位，囚禁諸王，但無縲紲耳。

translations.literal: Moreover, Emperor Wu of Wei loved Prince Si of Chen; when Emperor Wen succeeded, he imprisoned the princes—only without the cord and fetters.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Wei loved Prince Si of Chen; when Emperor Wen took the throne, he imprisoned the princes—only without putting them in bonds.

sentences.zh: 然則武帝愛之，適所以苦之也。

translations.literal: Thus Wu's love for him was precisely what made him suffer.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the father's love was precisely what brought the son to grief.

sentences.zh: 又，百姓所以治安，唯在刺史、縣令，苟選用得人，則陛下可以端拱無為。

translations.literal: Moreover, the people's peace and order depend solely on prefects and magistrates; if the right men are chosen, Your Majesty can sit upright with folded hands and do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the people's peace depends solely on prefects and magistrates; choose the right men and Your Majesty may rule with folded hands and do nothing.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷唯重內官而輕州縣之選，刺史多用武人，或京官不稱職始補外任，邊遠之處，用人更輕。

translations.literal: Now the court values only inner officials and treats selection for prefectures and counties lightly; prefects are mostly military men, or capital officials who proved unfit are sent out to fill external posts; in remote regions, men are chosen even more casually.
translations.idiomatic: Today the court values inner officials and treats provincial appointments lightly; most prefects are military men, or capital officials who failed at their posts are sent out to the provinces; in remote districts the appointments are even more careless.

sentences.zh: 所以百姓未安，殆由於此。」

translations.literal: That the people are not at peace is probably due to this."
translations.idiomatic: That the people are not at peace is probably due to this."

sentences.zh: 疏奏，上稱善久之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was presented, the emperor praised it at length.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was presented, the emperor praised it at length.

sentences.zh: 謂侍臣曰：「刺史，朕當自選；

translations.literal: He said to his attending officials: "For prefects, I shall choose them myself;
translations.idiomatic: He told his attendants: "I shall choose the prefects myself;

sentences.zh: 縣令，宜詔京官五品已上各舉一人。」

translations.literal: for magistrates, it is fitting to order capital officials of the fifth rank and above each to recommend one man."
translations.idiomatic: for magistrates, let every capital official of the fifth rank and above recommend one candidate."

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，癸丑，詔勳戚亡者皆陪葬山陵。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day gui-chou, an edict ordered that deceased meritorious kin and affines all be buried with the imperial tombs on the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the day gui-chou, an edict ordered that deceased meritorious kin and affines be buried in the imperial tombs on the mountain.

sentences.zh: 上獵於洛陽苑，有群豕突出林中，上引弓四發，殪四豕。

translations.literal: The emperor hunted in the Luoyang park. A herd of boars burst from the woods; the emperor drew his bow four times and killed four boars.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was hunting in the Luoyang park when a herd of boars burst from the woods. He loosed four arrows and killed four of them.

sentences.zh: 有豕突前，及馬鐙；

translations.literal: One boar charged forward and reached the horse's stirrup;
translations.idiomatic: One boar charged forward and reached the stirrup of his horse;

sentences.zh: 民部尚書唐儉投馬搏之，上拔劍斬豕，顧笑曰：「天策長史不見上將擊賊邪，何懼之甚！」

translations.literal: Minister of the Ministry for the People Tang Jian leaped from his horse to grapple it. The emperor drew his sword and slew the boar, then turned with a laugh and said: "Does the Chief Secretary of the Heavenly Stratagem Army not see a supreme commander striking the enemy—why so much fear!"
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the Ministry for the People Tang Jian leaped from his horse to grapple the beast. The emperor drew his sword and cut the boar down, then turned with a laugh and said: "Does the Chief Secretary of the Heavenly Stratagem Army not see a supreme commander striking down the enemy—why so much fear!"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「漢高祖以馬上得之，不以馬上治之；

translations.literal: He replied: "Emperor Gaozu of Han won the realm on horseback but did not govern it on horseback;
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Emperor Gaozu of Han won the realm on horseback but did not govern it on horseback;

sentences.zh: 陛下以神武定四方，豈復逞雄心於一獸！」

translations.literal: Your Majesty, with divine martial prowess, settled the four quarters—how could you still display fierce ambition against a single beast!"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, with divine martial prowess, settled the four quarters—why would you still vent your battle fury on a single beast!"

sentences.zh: 上悅，為之罷獵，尋加光祿大夫。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased, stopped the hunt on his account, and soon promoted him to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased, ended the hunt on his account, and soon promoted him to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 安州都督吳王恪數出畋獵，頗損居人；

translations.literal: Anzhou regional commander Prince Wu Li Ke went out hunting many times and considerably harmed the residents;
translations.idiomatic: Anzhou regional commander Prince Wu Li Ke went hunting repeatedly and caused considerable harm to local residents;

sentences.zh: 侍御史柳范奏彈之。

translations.literal: the attendant censor Liu Fan memorialized to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Censor Liu Fan memorialized to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，恪坐免官，削戶三百。

translations.literal: On the day ding-chou, Li Ke was punished by removal from office and reduction of three hundred households in his fief.
translations.idiomatic: On the day ding-chou, Li Ke was removed from office and stripped of three hundred households from his fief.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「長史權萬紀事吾兒，不能匡正，罪當死。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Chief Administrator Quan Wanji served my son yet could not correct him—his crime deserves death."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Chief Administrator Quan Wanji served my son yet failed to correct him—his crime deserves death."

sentences.zh: 柳范曰：「房玄齡事陛下，猶不能止畋獵，豈得獨罪萬紀！」

translations.literal: Liu Fan said: "Fang Xuanling served Your Majesty yet could not stop your hunting—how can Wanji alone be blamed!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fan said: "Fang Xuanling served Your Majesty yet could not stop your hunting—how can Wanji alone be blamed!"

sentences.zh: 上大怒，拂衣而入。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered, brushed his robes and went inside.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage, brushed his robes aside, and stalked off.

sentences.zh: 久之，獨引范謂曰：「何面折我？」

translations.literal: After a long while he summoned Liu Fan alone and said: "Why did you contradict me to my face?"
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he summoned Liu Fan alone and said: "Why did you contradict me to my face?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下仁明，臣不敢不盡愚直。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your Majesty is benevolent and clear-sighted; your servant dares not fail to exhaust blunt loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Your Majesty is benevolent and clear-sighted; I dared not withhold plain, loyal speech."

sentences.zh: 上悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 十一月，辛卯，上幸懷州；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day xin-mao, the emperor visited Huaizhou;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the day xin-mao, the emperor went to Huaizhou;

sentences.zh: 丙午，還洛陽宮。

translations.literal: On the day bing-wu, he returned to Luoyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bing-wu, he returned to Luoyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 故荊州都督武士擭女，年十四，上聞其美，召入後宮，為才人。

translations.literal: The daughter of the former Jingzhou regional commander Wu Shihuo, aged fourteen—when the emperor heard of her beauty, he summoned her into the rear palace and made her a cairen.
translations.idiomatic: The daughter of the former Jingzhou regional commander Wu Shihuo was fourteen years old. When the emperor heard of her beauty, he summoned her to the inner palace and made her a cairen.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙未，禮部尚書王珪奏：「三品已上遇親王於路皆降乘，非禮。」

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day yi-wei, Minister of Rites Wang Gui memorialized: "Officials of the third rank and above, when meeting imperial princes on the road, all dismount from their carriages—this is not according to ritual."
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the day yi-wei, Minister of Rites Wang Gui memorialized: "When officials of the third rank and above meet imperial princes on the road, they all dismount from their carriages—this is not proper ritual."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿輩苟自崇貴，輕我諸子。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You gentlemen presumptuously esteem yourselves noble and slight my sons."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "You presumptuously esteem yourselves and slight my sons."

sentences.zh: 特進魏徵曰：「諸王位次三公，今三品皆九卿、八座，為王降乘，誠非所宜當。」

translations.literal: Special Advancement Holder Wei Zheng said: "The princes rank below the Three Dukes; now the third rank are all nine ministers and eight seats—for them to dismount for princes is truly not what is fitting."
translations.idiomatic: Special Advancement Holder Wei Zheng said: "Imperial princes rank below the Three Dukes, while third-rank officials are the nine ministers and eight seats—for them to dismount for princes is truly inappropriate."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「人生壽夭難期，萬一太子不幸，安知諸王他日不為公輩之主！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Human life and death are hard to foresee; if by chance the crown prince should meet misfortune, who knows whether the princes may not one day become your masters!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Life and death are hard to foresee. If the crown prince should meet misfortune, who knows whether the princes may not one day become your masters!

sentences.zh: 何得輕之！」

translations.literal: How can you slight them!"
translations.idiomatic: How can you slight them!"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「自周以來，皆子孫相繼，不立兄弟，所以絕庶孽之窺窬，塞禍亂之源本，此為國者所深戒也。」

translations.literal: He replied: "From the Zhou onward, succession has always been from son to son, never establishing brothers—thereby cutting off the covetous glances of collateral lines and blocking the root sources of calamity and disorder. This is what those who govern a state must deeply guard against."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Since the Zhou, succession has always passed from father to son, never to a brother—thereby cutting off the ambitions of collateral lines and blocking the sources of rebellion. This is what every ruler must guard against most deeply."

sentences.zh: 上乃從珪奏。

translations.literal: The emperor then followed Wang Gui's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then accepted Wang Gui's memorial.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書高士廉、黃門侍郎韋挺、禮部侍郎令狐德葇、中書侍郎岑文本撰《氏族志》成，上之。

translations.literal: Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Gao Shilian, Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate Wei Ting, Vice Minister of Rites Linghu Defen, and Vice Director of the Secretariat Cen Wenben completed compilation of the Record of Clans and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Gao Shilian, Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate Wei Ting, Vice Minister of Rites Linghu Defen, and Vice Director of the Secretariat Cen Wenben completed the Record of Clans and presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 先是，山東人士崔、盧、李、鄭諸族，好自矜地望，雖累葉陵夷，苟他族欲與為昏姻，必多責財幣，或捨其鄉里而妄稱名族，或兄弟齊列而更以妻族相陵。

translations.literal: Earlier, among the gentry east of the mountains, the clans Cui, Lu, Li, and Zheng liked to pride themselves on their territorial standing; though generation after generation declined, if other clans wished to marry with them, they always demanded much wealth, or abandoned their native districts and falsely claimed famous clans, or brothers stood equal yet used their wives' clans to domineer over one another.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, among the eastern gentry, the Cui, Lu, Li, and Zheng clans prided themselves on their pedigree. Though their lines had declined for generations, any clan that sought marriage with them had to pay heavily; some abandoned their home districts to claim famous lineage falsely, and brothers of equal rank used their wives' clans to lord it over one another.

sentences.zh: 上惡之，命士廉等遍責天下譜諜，質諸史籍，考其真偽，辨其昭穆，第其甲乙，褒進忠賢，貶退奸逆，分為九等。

translations.literal: The emperor detested this and ordered Shilian and the others to collect genealogies throughout the realm, test them against historical records, examine truth and falsehood, distinguish senior and junior lines, rank them in grades of first and second class, promote the loyal and worthy and demote the treacherous and rebellious, dividing them into nine grades.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor detested this and ordered Shilian and the others to gather genealogies from across the realm, verify them against historical records, distinguish true from false and senior from junior lines, rank them in grades, promote the loyal and worthy and demote the treacherous and rebellious, and divide them into nine ranks.

sentences.zh: 士廉等以黃門侍郎崔民幹為第一。

translations.literal: Shilian and the others ranked Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate Cui Min'gan first.
translations.idiomatic: Shilian and the others ranked Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate Cui Min'gan first.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「漢高祖與蕭、曹、樊、灌皆起閭閻布衣，卿輩至今推仰，以為英賢，豈在世祿乎！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Emperor Gaozu of Han, with Xiao, Cao, Fan, and Guan, all rose from village lanes as commoners—yet you gentlemen still revere them to this day as heroic worthies. Was it because of hereditary stipends!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Emperor Gaozu of Han, along with Xiao He, Cao Shen, Fan Kuai, and Guan Ying, all rose from common village stock—yet you still revere them as heroic worthies. Was it because of hereditary office!

sentences.zh: 高氏偏據山東，梁、陳僻在江南，雖有人物，蓋何足言？

translations.literal: The Gao clan held only partial sway east of the mountains; Liang and Chen were remote in the south of the Yangtze—though they had men of talent, what were they worth mentioning!
translations.idiomatic: The Gao clan held only part of Shandong; Liang and Chen were confined to the south of the Yangtze—what were their men of talent worth mentioning!

sentences.zh: 況其子孫才行衰薄，官爵陵替，而猶卬然以門地自負，販鬻松檟，依托富貴，棄廉忘恥，不知世人何為貴之！

translations.literal: How much more when their descendants' conduct and talent have decayed and thinned, offices and ranks have declined and fallen, yet they still hold their heads high, proud of their clan status, selling their ancestral graves, relying on the rich and noble, casting off integrity and forgetting shame—one does not know why the world esteems them!
translations.idiomatic: Their descendants' talent and conduct have withered, their offices and ranks have fallen into decay—yet they still hold their heads high, proud of their pedigree, selling their ancestral graves, clinging to the rich and powerful, casting off integrity and shame. Why does the world still esteem them!

sentences.zh: 今三品以上，或以德行，或以勳勞，或以文學，致位貴顯。

translations.literal: Now those of the third rank and above have attained noble and eminent position through virtue and conduct, or through merit and toil, or through literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: Today those of the third rank and above have risen to eminence through virtue, merit, or literary accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 彼衰世舊門，誠何足慕！

translations.literal: Those old houses of a declining age—what are they truly worth admiring!
translations.idiomatic: Those decayed houses of a fallen age—what are they worth admiring!

sentences.zh: 而求與為昏，雖多輸金帛，猶為彼所偃蹇，我不知其解何也！

translations.literal: Yet in seeking marriage with them, though one pays much gold and silk, one is still put down by them—I do not understand the reason!
translations.idiomatic: Yet men seek marriage with them and pay heavily in gold and silk, only to be looked down upon—I cannot understand why!

sentences.zh: 今欲釐正訛謬，捨名取實，而卿曹猶以崔民幹為第一，是輕我官爵而徇流俗之情也。」

translations.literal: Now I wish to rectify errors and falsehoods, discard names and take reality—yet you gentlemen still place Cui Min'gan first. This is to slight my offices and ranks and follow the feelings of vulgar fashion."
translations.idiomatic: I wish to correct these errors, discard empty names for real merit—yet you still rank Cui Min'gan first. That is to slight my offices and cater to vulgar fashion."

sentences.zh: 乃更命刊定，專以今朝品秩為高下。

translations.literal: He then ordered a new revision, taking only the present court's ranks and grades as the standard of high and low.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered a new revision, ranking clans solely by present court rank.

sentences.zh: 於是以皇族為首，外戚次之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the imperial clan was placed first, maternal kin second.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial clan was placed first, maternal kin second.

sentences.zh: 降崔民幹為第三。

translations.literal: Cui Min'gan was lowered to third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Min'gan was lowered to third rank.

sentences.zh: 凡二百九十三姓，千六百五十一家，頒於天下。

translations.literal: Altogether two hundred ninety-three surnames and one thousand six hundred fifty-one households were promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In all, two hundred ninety-three surnames in one thousand six hundred fifty-one households were promulgated throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙卯，車駕西還；

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day yi-mao, the imperial carriage returned west;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day yi-mao, the emperor returned west;

sentences.zh: 癸亥，幸河北，觀砥柱。

translations.literal: on the day gui-hai, he visited Hebei and viewed the pillar rocks.
translations.idiomatic: on the day gui-hai, he went to Hebei to view the pillar rocks in the river.

sentences.zh: 甲子，巫州獠反，夔州都督齊善行敗之，俘男女三千餘口。

translations.literal: On the day jia-zi, the Liao of Wuzhou rebelled; Qizhou regional commander Qi Shanshang defeated them and captured more than three thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jia-zi, the Liao of Wuzhou rebelled. Qizhou regional commander Qi Shanshang defeated them and took more than three thousand captives, men and women.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，上祀禹廟。

translations.literal: On the day yi-chou, the emperor sacrificed at the temple of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yi-chou, the emperor sacrificed at the temple of Yu the Great.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，至柳谷，觀鹽池。

translations.literal: On the day ding-mao, he reached Willow Valley and viewed the salt ponds.
translations.idiomatic: On the day ding-mao, he reached Willow Valley and inspected the salt ponds.

sentences.zh: 庚午，至蒲州，刺史趙元楷課父老服黃紗單衣迎車駕，盛飾廨捨樓觀，又飼羊百餘口、魚數百頭以饋貴戚。

translations.literal: On the day geng-wu, he reached Puzhou. Prefect Zhao Yuankai compelled the elders to wear yellow gauze single garments to welcome the imperial carriage, lavishly decorated the government offices and towers, and moreover raised more than a hundred sheep and several hundred fish to present to noble kin.
translations.idiomatic: On the day geng-wu, he reached Puzhou. Prefect Zhao Yuankai forced the local elders to wear yellow gauze single garments to welcome the imperial procession, lavishly decorated the government offices and towers, and raised more than a hundred sheep and several hundred fish to present to the emperor's kin.

sentences.zh: 上數之曰：「朕巡省河、洛，凡有所須，皆資庫物。

translations.literal: The emperor reproached him, saying: "When I tour and inspect the Yellow and Luo rivers, whatever I need is all supplied from the treasury stores.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked him: "When I tour the Yellow and Luo region, whatever I need comes from the treasury.

sentences.zh: 卿所為乃亡隋之弊俗也。」

translations.literal: What you have done is the corrupt custom of the fallen Sui."
translations.idiomatic: What you have done is the corrupt custom of the fallen Sui."

sentences.zh: 甲戌，幸長春宮。

translations.literal: On the day jia-xu, he visited Everlasting Spring Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jia-xu, he went to Everlasting Spring Palace.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，詔曰：「隋故鷹擊郎將堯君素，雖桀犬吠堯，有乖倒戈之志，而疾風勁草，實表歲寒之心；

translations.literal: On the day wu-yin, an edict stated: "The former Sui Eagle-Strike Commandant Yao Junsu, though like Jie's dog barking at Yao, was at odds with the will to turn one's spear—yet like strong wind and stiff grass, he truly showed a heart for the year's cold;
translations.idiomatic: On the day wu-yin, an edict stated: "The former Sui Eagle-Strike Commandant Yao Junsu, though he stood against the tide like Jie's dog barking at Yao and refused to turn his spear, showed the steadfast heart of the grass that bends only in the fiercest wind;

sentences.zh: 可贈蒲州刺史，仍訪其子孫以聞。」

translations.literal: he may be posthumously appointed Prefect of Puzhou, and his descendants are still to be sought out and reported."
translations.idiomatic: let him be posthumously appointed Prefect of Puzhou, and let his descendants be sought out and reported."

sentences.zh: 閏月，庚辰朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on the first day of the month geng-chen, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on the first day geng-chen, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 丁未，車駕至京師。

translations.literal: On the day ding-wei, the imperial carriage reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the day ding-wei, the emperor reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 三月，辛亥，著作佐郎鄧世隆表請集上文章。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day xin-hai, Assistant Editorial Director Deng Shilong memorialized requesting that the emperor's writings be collected.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day xin-hai, Assistant Editorial Director Deng Shilong memorialized asking that the emperor's writings be collected.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕之辭令，有益於民者，史皆書之，足為不朽。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "My edicts and commands that benefit the people are all recorded by the historians—this is enough for immortality.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "My edicts that benefit the people are all recorded by the historians—that is immortality enough.

sentences.zh: 若其無益，集之何用！

translations.literal: If they are not beneficial, what use is collecting them!
translations.idiomatic: If they are not beneficial, what use is collecting them!

sentences.zh: 梁武帝父子、陳後主、隋煬帝皆有文集行於世，何救於亡！

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang and his son, Emperor Houzhu of Chen, and Emperor Yang of Sui all had collected works circulating in the world—what did that avail against their fall!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang and his son, Emperor Houzhu of Chen, and Emperor Yang of Sui all had literary collections in circulation—what did that avail against their ruin!

sentences.zh: 為人主患無德政，文章何為！」

translations.literal: What a ruler should fear is lack of virtuous government—what are literary compositions for!"
translations.idiomatic: What a ruler should fear is lack of virtuous government—what are literary compositions for!"

sentences.zh: 遂不許。

translations.literal: He thereupon did not grant permission.
translations.idiomatic: He refused the request.

sentences.zh: 丙子，以皇孫生，宴五品以上於東宮。

translations.literal: On the day bing-zi, because an imperial grandson was born, he feasted officials of the fifth rank and above at the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bing-zi, because an imperial grandson had been born, the emperor feasted officials of the fifth rank and above at the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「貞觀之前，從朕經營天下，玄齡之功也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Before Zhenguan, in following me to build the realm, it was Xuanling's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Before the Zhenguan era, in building the realm with me, the credit belongs to Xuanling.

sentences.zh: 貞觀以來，繩愆糾繆，魏徵之功也。」

translations.literal: Since Zhenguan, in binding faults and correcting errors, it has been Wei Zheng's achievement."
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhenguan, in binding faults and correcting errors, the credit belongs to Wei Zheng."

sentences.zh: 皆賜之佩刀。

translations.literal: Both were granted belt swords.
translations.idiomatic: He granted belt swords to both.

sentences.zh: 上謂征曰：「朕政事何如往年？」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Zheng: "How does my governance compare with former years?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Zheng: "How does my governance compare with former years?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「威德所加，比貞觀之初則遠矣；

translations.literal: He replied: "The majesty and virtue you extend are far greater than at the beginning of Zhenguan;
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "The majesty and virtue you extend are far greater than at the beginning of Zhenguan;

sentences.zh: 人悅服則不逮也。」

translations.literal: but in winning people's willing submission, you do not measure up."
translations.idiomatic: but in winning the people's willing hearts, you do not measure up."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「遠方畏威慕德，故來服；

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Distant regions fear our majesty and admire our virtue, and therefore come to submit;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Distant lands fear our majesty and admire our virtue, and therefore submit;

sentences.zh: 若其不逮，何以致之？」

translations.literal: if I do not measure up, how did this come about?"
translations.idiomatic: if I do not measure up in their hearts, how did that come about?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下往以未治為憂，故德義日新；

translations.literal: He replied: "Your Majesty formerly took lack of good order as your worry, and therefore virtue and righteousness renewed day by day;
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Your Majesty formerly worried that the realm was not well governed, and therefore your virtue renewed itself day by day;

sentences.zh: 今以既治為安，故不逮。」

translations.literal: now you take already being governed as security, and therefore you do not measure up."
translations.idiomatic: now you take the realm as already well governed and rest secure, and therefore you do not measure up."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「今所為，猶往年也，何以異？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What I do now is still as in former years—how is it different?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "What I do now is the same as in former years—how is it different?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下貞觀之初，恐人不諫，常導之使言，中間悅而從之。

translations.literal: He replied: "At the beginning of Zhenguan, Your Majesty feared that people would not remonstrate and constantly guided them to speak; in the middle period you were pleased and followed their advice.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "At the beginning of Zhenguan, Your Majesty feared that no one would speak up and constantly encouraged remonstrance; in the middle period you were pleased and followed good counsel.

sentences.zh: 今則不然，雖勉從之，猶有難色。

translations.literal: Now it is not so—even when you force yourself to follow, you still show a troubled expression.
translations.idiomatic: Now it is not so—even when you force yourself to comply, your face still shows reluctance.

sentences.zh: 所以異也。」

translations.literal: This is how it differs."
translations.idiomatic: That is the difference."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「其事可聞歟？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Can the matter be told?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Can you give an example?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下昔欲殺元律師，孫伏伽以為法不當死，陛下賜以蘭陵公主園，直百萬。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your Majesty once wished to execute Yuan Lüshi; Sun Fuga held that by law he should not die, and Your Majesty bestowed on him the park of Princess Lanling, worth a million.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Your Majesty once wished to execute Yuan Lüshi. Sun Fuga argued that the law did not require death, and Your Majesty bestowed on him the park of Princess Lanling, worth a million cash.

sentences.zh: 或云：『賞太厚。』

translations.literal: Some said: 'The reward is too generous.'
translations.idiomatic: Some said: 'The reward is too generous.'

sentences.zh: 陛下云：『朕即位以來，未有諫者，故賞之。』

translations.literal: Your Majesty said: 'Since I took the throne, there has been no remonstrator—therefore I reward him.'
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty said: 'Since I took the throne, there has been no one who remonstrated—therefore I reward him.'

sentences.zh: 此導之使言也。

translations.literal: This was guiding them to speak.
translations.idiomatic: That was encouraging remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 司戶柳雄妄訴隋資，陛下欲誅之，納戴冑之諫而止。

translations.literal: Director of Households Liu Xiong falsely claimed Sui-era credentials; Your Majesty wished to execute him but accepted Dai Zhou's remonstrance and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Households Liu Xiong falsely claimed Sui-era credentials. Your Majesty wished to execute him but accepted Dai Zhou's remonstrance and stopped.

sentences.zh: 是悅而從之也。

translations.literal: This was being pleased and following advice.
translations.idiomatic: That was being pleased and following good counsel.

sentences.zh: 近皇甫德參上書諫修洛陽宮，陛下恚之，雖以臣言而罷，勉從之也。」

translations.literal: Recently Huangfu Decan memorialized against repairing Luoyang Palace; Your Majesty was angry. Though you stopped on my words, you followed only with reluctance."
translations.idiomatic: Recently Huangfu Decan memorialized against repairing Luoyang Palace. Your Majesty was angry. Though you stopped on my advice, you complied only with reluctance."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「非公不能及此。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Without you, I could not have reached this insight.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Without you, I could not have seen this so clearly.

sentences.zh: 人苦不自知耳！」

translations.literal: How bitter it is that people do not know themselves!"
translations.idiomatic: How hard it is for a man to know himself!"

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，壬申，弘文館學士永興文懿公虞世南卒，上哭之慟。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on the day ren-shen, Hongwen Hall academician the Duke of Literary Excellence of Yongxing Yu Shinan died; the emperor wept for him bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on the day ren-shen, Hongwen Hall academician Yu Shinan, Duke of Literary Excellence of Yongxing, died. The emperor wept bitterly for him.

sentences.zh: 世南外和柔而內忠直，上嘗稱世南有五絕：一德行，二忠直，三博學，四文辭，五書翰。

translations.literal: Shinan was outwardly gentle and yielding but inwardly loyal and upright. The emperor once praised that Shinan had five supreme excellences: first, virtue and conduct; second, loyalty and uprightness; third, broad learning; fourth, literary composition; fifth, calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: Shinan was outwardly gentle but inwardly loyal and upright. The emperor once said Shinan had five supreme gifts: virtue, loyalty, broad learning, literary skill, and calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸酉，以吏部尚書高士廉為右僕射。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day gui-you, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Gao Shilian was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day gui-you, Minister of Personnel Gao Shilian was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，吐蕃寇弘州。

translations.literal: On the day yi-hai, the Tibetans raided Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yi-hai, the Tibetans raided Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 八月，霸州山獠反，燒殺刺史向邵陵及吏民百餘家。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the mountain Liao of Bazhou rebelled, burning and killing Prefect Xiang Shaoling and more than a hundred households of officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, the mountain Liao of Bazhou rebelled, burning and killing Prefect Xiang Shaoling and more than a hundred households of officials and commoners.

sentences.zh: 初，上遣使者馮德遐撫慰吐蕃，吐蕃聞突厥、吐谷渾皆尚公主，遣使隨德遐入朝，多繼金寶，奉表求婚；

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor sent the envoy Feng Dexia to console and comfort the Tibetans. The Tibetans heard that both the Turks and the Tuyuhun had been granted imperial princesses in marriage; they sent envoys following Dexia to court, bearing much gold and treasure, and presented a memorial requesting marriage;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the emperor had sent the envoy Feng Dexia to console the Tibetans. Hearing that both the Turks and the Tuyuhun had received imperial princesses in marriage, the Tibetans sent envoys to follow Dexia to court laden with gold and treasure and presented a memorial requesting a princess;

sentences.zh: 上未之許。

translations.literal: the emperor did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor did not grant the request.

sentences.zh: 使者還，言於贊普棄宗弄贊曰：「臣初至唐，唐待我甚厚，許尚公主。

translations.literal: When the envoys returned, they spoke to the tsenpo Songtsen Gampo: "When your servant first reached Tang, Tang treated us very generously and promised a princess in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys returned, they told the tsenpo Songtsen Gampo: "When I first reached Tang, they treated us very generously and promised a princess.

sentences.zh: 會吐谷渾王入朝，相離間，唐禮遂衰，亦不許婚。」

translations.literal: It happened that the king of the Tuyuhun came to court and sowed discord between us; Tang courtesy then declined, and they also would not grant marriage."
translations.idiomatic: Then the king of the Tuyuhun came to court and sowed discord between us. Tang courtesy then declined, and they refused the marriage as well."

sentences.zh: 弄贊遂發兵擊吐谷渾。

translations.literal: Gampo thereupon sent troops to attack the Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: Gampo thereupon sent troops to attack the Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾不能支，遁於青海之北，民畜多為吐蕃所掠。

translations.literal: The Tuyuhun could not withstand them and fled north of Qinghai Lake; many of their people and livestock were plundered by the Tibetans.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun could not withstand them and fled north of Qinghai Lake; much of their population and livestock was plundered by the Tibetans.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃進破党項、白蘭諸羌，帥眾二十餘萬屯松州西境，遣使貢金帛，雲來迎公主。

translations.literal: The Tibetans advanced and broke the Tangut, Bailan, and other Qiang tribes, leading more than two hundred thousand men to encamp on the western border of Songzhou, and sent envoys presenting gold and silk, saying they had come to welcome the princess.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans advanced, defeated the Tangut, Bailan, and other Qiang tribes, and camped on Songzhou's western border with more than two hundred thousand men. They sent envoys bearing gold and silk, saying they had come to welcome the princess.

sentences.zh: 尋進攻松州，敗都督韓威；

translations.literal: Soon they advanced to attack Songzhou and defeated regional commander Han Wei;
translations.idiomatic: Soon they attacked Songzhou and defeated regional commander Han Wei;

sentences.zh: 羌酋閻州刺史別叢臥施、諾州刺史把利步利並以州叛歸之。

translations.literal: the Qiang chieftains Yanzhou Prefect Bie Congwoshi and Nuozhou Prefect Bali Buli both rebelled with their prefectures and submitted to them.
translations.idiomatic: the Qiang chieftains Yanzhou Prefect Bie Congwoshi and Nuozhou Prefect Bali Buli both rebelled with their prefectures and submitted to the Tibetans.

sentences.zh: 連兵不息，其大臣諫不聽而自縊者凡八輩。

translations.literal: War continued without cease; eight of their great ministers who remonstrated but were not heeded hanged themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting continued without cease; eight of their ministers who remonstrated in vain hanged themselves.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，以吏部尚書侯君集為當彌道行軍大總管，甲辰，以右領軍大將軍執失思力為白蘭道、左武衛將軍牛進達為闊水道、左領軍將軍劉簡為洮河道行軍總管，督步騎五萬擊之。

translations.literal: On the day ren-yin, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Hou Junji was made Grand Marshal of the Dangmi Campaign Route; on the day jia-chen, Right General of the Rear Guard Zhishi Sili was made commander of the Bailan Route, Left General of the Martial Guard Niu Jinda commander of the Kuoshui Route, and Left General of the Front Guard Liu Jian commander of the Taohe River Route, supervising fifty thousand infantry and cavalry to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: On the day ren-yin, Minister of Personnel Hou Junji was appointed Grand Marshal of the Dangmi campaign route. On the day jia-chen, Right General of the Rear Guard Zhishi Sili was made commander of the Bailan route, Left General of the Martial Guard Niu Jinda commander of the Kuoshui route, and Left General of the Front Guard Liu Jian commander of the Taohe route, with fifty thousand infantry and cavalry to strike the Tibetans.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃攻城十餘日，進達為先鋒，九月，辛亥，掩其不備，敗吐蕃於松州城下，斬首千餘級。

translations.literal: The Tibetans besieged the city for more than ten days. Jinda served as vanguard; in the ninth month, on the day xin-hai, he caught them unprepared and defeated the Tibetans below Songzhou city, beheading more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans besieged Songzhou for more than ten days. Jinda served as vanguard; in the ninth month, on the day xin-hai, he caught them unprepared and defeated the Tibetans below the walls of Songzhou, beheading more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 弄贊懼，引兵退，遣使謝罪，因復請婚；

translations.literal: Gampo was afraid, withdrew his troops, sent envoys to apologize for his offense, and again requested marriage;
translations.idiomatic: Gampo was afraid, withdrew his troops, sent envoys to apologize, and again requested a princess;

sentences.zh: 上許之。

translations.literal: the emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor granted the request.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，上問侍臣：「帝王創業與守成孰難？」

translations.literal: On the day jia-yin, the emperor asked his attending officials: "For an emperor, which is harder—founding the enterprise or preserving what has been achieved?"
translations.idiomatic: On the day jia-yin, the emperor asked his attendants: "For an emperor, which is harder—founding the realm or preserving what has been achieved?"

sentences.zh: 房玄齡曰：「草昧之初，與群雄並起角力而後臣之，創業難矣。」

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling said: "At the beginning in the wilds, one rises with the heroes, struggles in contest, and only afterward makes them subjects—founding is hard."
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling said: "In the beginning, when the realm was still unsettled, one contended with rival heroes and only afterward made them subjects—founding is the harder task."

sentences.zh: 魏徵曰：「自古帝王，莫不得之於艱難，失之於安逸，守成難矣。」

translations.literal: Wei Zheng said: "From antiquity, no emperor has failed to gain the realm through hardship and lose it through ease and comfort—preserving what has been achieved is hard."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng said: "Throughout history, emperors have won their realms through hardship and lost them through ease—preserving what has been achieved is the harder task."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「玄齡與吾共取天下，出百死，得一生，故知創業之難。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Xuanling and I together took the realm—out of a hundred deaths, one life—therefore he knows the hardship of founding.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Xuanling and I together won the realm—out of a hundred deaths, one life—so he knows how hard founding was.

sentences.zh: 征與吾共安天下，常恐驕奢生於富貴，禍亂生於所忽，故知守成之難。

translations.literal: Zheng and I together have settled the realm; I constantly fear that arrogance and extravagance arise from wealth and honor, and calamity and disorder arise from what is neglected—therefore he knows the hardship of preserving.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng and I together have settled the realm. I constantly fear that arrogance and extravagance arise from wealth and honor, and that calamity arises from what is neglected—so he knows how hard preserving is.

sentences.zh: 然創業之難，既已往矣，守成之難，方當與諸公慎之。」

translations.literal: Yet the hardship of founding is already past; the hardship of preserving—we must now be careful of it together with you gentlemen."
translations.idiomatic: The hardship of founding is already past; the hardship of preserving is what we must now guard against together."

sentences.zh: 玄齡等拜曰：「陛下及此言，四海之福也。」

translations.literal: Xuanling and the others bowed and said: "Your Majesty has reached these words—the blessing of the four seas."
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling and the others bowed and said: "Your Majesty has spoken these words—the blessing of the four seas."

sentences.zh: 初，突厥頡利既亡，北方空虛，薛延陀真珠可汗帥其部落建庭於都尉犍山北、獨邏水南，勝兵二十萬，立其二子拔酌、頡利苾主南、北部。

translations.literal: Earlier, after the Turkic Jiali Khan perished, the north was empty. The Xueyantuo Khan Zhenzhu led his tribes to establish a court north of Commander's Qilian Mountain and south of the Toluo River, with two hundred thousand effective troops, and installed his two sons Bazhuo and Jielibi to govern the southern and northern parts.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after the Turkic Jiali Khan fell, the north lay empty. The Xueyantuo Khan Zhenzhu led his tribes to establish a court north of Commander's Qilian Mountain and south of the Toluo River with two hundred thousand fighting men, and installed his sons Bazhuo and Jielibi to govern the southern and northern wings.

sentences.zh: 上以其強盛，恐後難制，癸亥，拜其二子皆為小可汗，各賜鼓纛，外示優崇，實分其勢。

translations.literal: The emperor, because they were strong and flourishing, feared they would later be hard to control. On the day gui-hai, he invested both sons as lesser khans, each bestowing drums and banners—outwardly showing favor and honor, but in reality dividing their power.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing their strength would later prove hard to control, on the day gui-hai the emperor invested both sons as lesser khans, each bestowing drums and banners—outwardly showing honor, but in reality dividing their power.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，乙亥，巴州獠反。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day yi-hai, the Liao of Bazhou rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the day yi-hai, the Liao of Bazhou rebelled.

sentences.zh: 己卯，畋於始平；

translations.literal: On the day ji-mao, he hunted at Shiping;
translations.idiomatic: On the day ji-mao, the emperor went hunting at Shiping;

sentences.zh: 乙未，還京師。

translations.literal: On the day yi-wei, he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yi-wei, he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 鈞州獠反；

translations.literal: The Liao of Junzhou rebelled;
translations.idiomatic: The Liao tribes of Junzhou rebelled;

sentences.zh: 遣桂州都督張寶德討平之。

translations.literal: He dispatched Zhang Baode, regional inspector of Guizhou, to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched Zhang Baode, regional inspector of Guizhou, to suppress and pacify them.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丁未，初置左、右屯營飛騎於玄武門，以諸將軍領之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day ding-wei, the Left and Right Garrison Flying Cavalry were first established at the Xuanwu Gate, with various generals placed in command.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the day ding-wei, the Left and Right Garrison Flying Cavalry were first established at the Xuanwu Gate, with various generals placed in command.

sentences.zh: 又簡飛騎才力驍健、善騎射者，號百騎，衣五色袍，乘駿馬，以虎皮為韉，凡游幸則從焉。

translations.literal: Flying cavalry of exceptional strength and skill in riding and shooting were also selected, called the Hundred Riders; they wore robes of five colors, rode fine horses, and used tiger skins for saddles, accompanying him on all excursions.
translations.idiomatic: Elite flying cavalry noted for strength, valor, and skill in riding and shooting were also chosen and called the Hundred Riders. They wore robes of five colors, rode fine horses, and used tiger skins for saddles, accompanying the emperor on all excursions.

sentences.zh: 己巳，明州獠反；

translations.literal: On the day ji-si, the Liao of Mingzhou rebelled;
translations.idiomatic: On the day ji-si, the Liao tribes of Mingzhou rebelled;

sentences.zh: 遣交州都督李道彥討平之。

translations.literal: He dispatched Li Daoyan, regional inspector of Jiaozhou, to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched Li Daoyan, regional inspector of Jiaozhou, to suppress and pacify them.

sentences.zh: 十二月，辛巳，左武候將軍上官懷仁擊反獠於壁州，大破之，虜男女萬餘口。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day xin-si, Left Martial Guard General Shangguan Huairen attacked the rebel Liao at Bizhou, defeating them utterly and capturing more than ten thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day xin-si, Left Martial Guard General Shangguan Huairen attacked the rebel Liao at Bizhou, routing them and capturing more than ten thousand men and women.

sentences.zh: 是歲，以給事中馬周為中書舍人。

translations.literal: That year, Ma Zhou, supervisory secretary in the Secretariat, was made a drafting secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Ma Zhou, a supervisory secretary in the Secretariat, was appointed drafting secretary of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 周有機辯，中書侍郎嶺岑文本常稱：「馬君論事，援引事類，揚榷古今，舉要刪煩，會文切理，一字不可增，亦不可減，聽之靡靡，令人忘倦。」

translations.literal: Zhou had quick wit and eloquence. Vice Director of the Secretariat Cen Wenben often said: "When Master Ma discusses affairs, he cites parallels from past and present, sifting through antiquity and the present day, selecting essentials and cutting redundancy, joining words to precise reason—not a character could be added, nor could one be removed. Listening to him is utterly entrancing; one forgets weariness."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou was quick-witted and eloquent. Vice Director of the Secretariat Cen Wenben often said: "When Master Ma discusses affairs, he cites parallels from past and present, sifting antiquity and the present, selecting essentials and cutting redundancy, joining words to precise reason—not a character could be added or removed. Listening to him is utterly entrancing; one forgets weariness."

sentences.zh: 霍王元軌好讀書，恭謹自守，舉措不妄。

translations.literal: Prince Huo Yuan Gui loved reading books, was respectful and cautious in self-restraint, and did nothing rash in conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huo Yuan Gui loved reading, was respectful and cautious in self-restraint, and never acted rashly.

sentences.zh: 為徐州刺史，與處士劉玄平為布衣交。

translations.literal: As regional inspector of Xuzhou, he formed a friendship as common men with the reclusive scholar Liu Xuanping.
translations.idiomatic: As regional inspector of Xuzhou, he formed a friendship as equals with the reclusive scholar Liu Xuanping.

sentences.zh: 人問玄平王所長，玄平曰：「無長。」

translations.literal: Someone asked Xuanping what the prince's strengths were. Xuanping said: "None."
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked Xuanping what the prince's strengths were. Xuanping said: "None."

sentences.zh: 問者怪之。

translations.literal: The questioner found this strange.
translations.idiomatic: The questioner found this strange.

sentences.zh: 玄平曰：「夫人有所短乃見所長，至於霍王，無所短，吾何以稱其長哉！」

translations.literal: Xuanping said: "When a man has shortcomings, his strengths become visible. As for Prince Huo, he has no shortcomings—how am I to name his strengths!"
translations.idiomatic: Xuanping said: "When a man has shortcomings, his strengths become visible. As for Prince Huo, he has no shortcomings—how am I to name his strengths!"

sentences.zh: 初，西突厥咥利失可汗分其國為十部，每部有酋長一人，仍各賜一箭，謂之十箭。

translations.literal: Previously, the Western Turkic khagan Dilishi divided his realm into ten divisions; each division had one chieftain, and each was further given one arrow—they were called the Ten Arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, the Western Turkic khagan Dilishi divided his realm into ten divisions. Each had one chieftain, and each was given one arrow—they were called the Ten Arrows.

sentences.zh: 又分左、右廂，左廂號五咄陸，置五大啜，居碎葉以東；

translations.literal: They were further divided into left and right wings: the left wing was called the Five Tulu, with five great jurors established, dwelling east of Suyab;
translations.idiomatic: They were further divided into left and right wings. The left wing was called the Five Tulu, with five great jurors established east of Suyab;

sentences.zh: 右廂號五弩失畢，置五大俟斤，居碎葉以西；

translations.literal: the right wing was called the Five Nushibi, with five great irkins established, dwelling west of Suyab;
translations.idiomatic: the right wing was called the Five Nushibi, with five great irkins established west of Suyab;

sentences.zh: 通謂之十姓。

translations.literal: collectively called the Ten Clans.
translations.idiomatic: They were collectively called the Ten Clans.

sentences.zh: 咥利失失眾心，為其臣統吐屯所襲。

translations.literal: Dilishi lost the hearts of the people and was attacked by his minister Tong Tutun.
translations.idiomatic: Dilishi lost the hearts of the people and was attacked by his minister Tong Tutun.

sentences.zh: 咥利失兵敗，與其弟步利設走保焉耆。

translations.literal: Dilishi's army was defeated; he and his younger brother Bulishi fled to take refuge in Yanqi.
translations.idiomatic: Dilishi's army was defeated; he and his younger brother Bulishi fled to take refuge in Yanqi.

sentences.zh: 統吐屯等將立欲谷設為大可汁，會統吐屯為人所殺，欲谷設兵亦敗，咥利失復得故地。

translations.literal: Tong Tutun and others were about to install Yugu She as great khan; but Tong Tutun was killed by someone, Yugu She's army was also defeated, and Dilishi recovered his former territory.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Tutun and others were about to install Yugu She as great khan; but Tong Tutun was killed, Yugu She's army was also defeated, and Dilishi recovered his former territory.

sentences.zh: 至是，西部竟立欲谷設為乙毘咄陸可汗。

translations.literal: By this time, the western tribes finally installed Yugu She as Khagan Yipiduolu.
translations.idiomatic: By this time, the western tribes finally installed Yugu She as Khagan Yipiduolu.

sentences.zh: 乙毘咄陸既立，與咥利失大戰，殺傷甚眾。

translations.literal: Once Yipiduolu was established, he fought a great battle with Dilishi, with many killed and wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yipiduolu was established, he fought a great battle with Dilishi, with heavy casualties on both sides.

sentences.zh: 因中分其地，自伊列水以西屬乙咄陸，以東屬咥利失。

translations.literal: Thereupon they divided the land between them: from the Ili River west belonged to Yipiduolu, and east belonged to Dilishi.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they divided the land between them: west of the Ili River belonged to Yipiduolu, and east of it to Dilishi.

sentences.zh: 處月、處密與高昌共攻拔焉耆五城，掠男女一千五百人，焚其廬舍而去。

translations.literal: The Chuyue, Chumi, and Gaochang jointly attacked and captured five cities of Yanqi, seizing fifteen hundred men and women, burning their dwellings, and departing.
translations.idiomatic: The Chuyue, Chumi, and Gaochang jointly attacked and captured five cities of Yanqi, seizing fifteen hundred men and women, burning their dwellings, and withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙巳，車駕謁獻陵；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day yi-si, the imperial carriage visited Xianling;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the day yi-si, the imperial carriage visited Xianling;

sentences.zh: 丁未，還宮。

translations.literal: on the day ding-wei, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the day ding-wei, he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 戊午，加左僕射房玄齡太子少師。

translations.literal: On the day wu-wu, Left Vice Grand Director Fang Xuanling was additionally appointed Junior Preceptor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wu-wu, Left Vice Grand Director Fang Xuanling was additionally appointed Junior Preceptor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 玄齡自以居端揆十五年，男遺愛尚上女高陽公主，女為韓王妃，深畏滿盈，上表請解機務；

translations.literal: Xuanling considered that he had held the highest office for fifteen years, that his son Yi'ai had married the emperor's daughter Princess Gaoyang, and that his daughter was consort to the Prince of Han; deeply fearing that fullness would bring overflow, he submitted a memorial requesting release from state affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling considered that he had held the highest office for fifteen years, that his son Yi'ai had married the emperor's daughter Princess Gaoyang, and that his daughter was consort to the Prince of Han. Deeply fearing that fullness would bring overflow, he submitted a memorial requesting release from state affairs;

sentences.zh: 上不許。

translations.literal: the emperor did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not grant the request.

sentences.zh: 玄齡固請不已，詔斷表，乃就職。

translations.literal: Xuanling repeatedly pressed his request without cease; an edict rejected his memorial, and he then took up his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling pressed his request repeatedly; an edict rejected his memorial, and he then took up his duties.

sentences.zh: 太子欲拜玄齡，設儀衛待之，玄齡不敢謁見而歸，時人美其有讓。

translations.literal: The crown prince wished to pay obeisance to Xuanling and set out ceremonial guards to receive him; Xuanling did not dare to attend an audience and returned home; contemporaries praised his humility.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince wished to pay obeisance to Xuanling and set out ceremonial guards to receive him. Xuanling did not dare to attend an audience and returned home; contemporaries praised his humility.

sentences.zh: 玄齡以度支系天下利害，嘗有闕，求其人未得，乃自領之。

translations.literal: Xuanling considered that the Directorate of Revenue was tied to the welfare of the realm; when there was once a vacancy and a suitable person could not be found, he took charge of it himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling considered that the Directorate of Revenue bore on the welfare of the realm. When a vacancy arose and no suitable person could be found, he took charge of it himself.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書永寧懿公王珪薨。
