translations.literal: Wang Gui, Minister of Rites and Duke Yi of Yongning, died.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui, Minister of Rites and Duke Yi of Yongning, died.

sentences.zh: 珪性寬裕，自奉養甚薄。

translations.literal: Gui was generous by nature and lived very modestly.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was generous by nature and lived very modestly.

sentences.zh: 於今，三品已上皆立家廟，珪通貴已久，獨祭於寢。

translations.literal: By now all officials of third rank and above had established ancestral temples; Gui had been prominent for a long time yet worshipped alone in his bedchamber.
translations.idiomatic: By now all officials of third rank and above had established ancestral temples. Gui had been prominent for a long time yet worshipped alone in his bedchamber.

sentences.zh: 為法司所劾，上不問，命有司為之立廟以愧之。

translations.literal: He was impeached by the legal authorities; the emperor did not inquire into it but ordered the relevant offices to build a temple for him as a rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: He was impeached by the legal authorities. The emperor did not pursue the matter but ordered the relevant offices to build a temple for him as a rebuke.

sentences.zh: 二月，庚辰，以光祿大夫尉遲敬德為鄜州都督。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day geng-chen, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Yuchi Jingde was made regional inspector of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day geng-chen, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Yuchi Jingde was appointed regional inspector of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 上嘗謂敬德曰：「人或言卿反，何也？」

translations.literal: The emperor once said to Jingde: "Some say you have rebelled—why?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once said to Jingde: "Some say you have rebelled—why?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣反是實！

translations.literal: He replied: "Your subject's rebellion is indeed true!
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Your subject's rebellion is indeed true!

sentences.zh: 臣從陛下征伐四方，身經百戰，今之存者，皆鋒鏑之餘也。

translations.literal: Your subject followed Your Majesty in campaigns across the four directions, personally enduring a hundred battles; those who survive today are what remains after blades and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject followed Your Majesty in campaigns across the four directions and personally endured a hundred battles. Those who survive today are what remains after blades and arrows.

sentences.zh: 天下已定，乃更疑臣反乎！」

translations.literal: The realm is already settled—yet you still suspect your subject of rebellion!"
translations.idiomatic: The realm is already settled—yet you still suspect your subject of rebellion!"

sentences.zh: 因解衣投地，出其瘢痍。

translations.literal: Thereupon he stripped off his clothes and cast them to the ground, exposing his scars.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he stripped off his clothes and cast them to the ground, exposing his scars.

sentences.zh: 上為之流涕，曰：「卿復服，朕不疑卿，故語卿，何更恨邪！」

translations.literal: The emperor wept for him and said: "Put your clothes back on. I do not doubt you—that is why I spoke to you. Why harbor resentment!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept for him and said: "Put your clothes back on. I do not doubt you—that is why I spoke to you. Why harbor resentment!"

sentences.zh: 上又嘗謂敬德曰：「朕欲以女妻卿，何如？」

translations.literal: The emperor also once said to Jingde: "I wish to give you my daughter in marriage—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also once said to Jingde: "I wish to give you my daughter in marriage—what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 敬德叩頭謝曰：「臣妻雖鄙陋，相與共貧賤久矣。

translations.literal: Jingde kowtowed and declined: "Though my wife is plain, we have shared poverty together for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde kowtowed and declined: "Though my wife is plain, we have shared poverty together for a long time.

sentences.zh: 臣雖不學，聞古人富不易妻，此非臣所願也。」

translations.literal: Though your subject is unlearned, I have heard that the ancients did not abandon their wives when they grew rich—this is not what your subject wishes."
translations.idiomatic: Though your subject is unlearned, I have heard that the ancients did not abandon their wives when they grew rich—this is not what your subject wishes."

sentences.zh: 上乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then desisted.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，尚書奏：「近世掖庭之選，或微賤之族，禮訓蔑聞；

translations.literal: On the day wu-xu, the Ministry submitted: "In recent times in selecting women for the inner quarters, some come from humble families with no training in ritual or instruction;
translations.idiomatic: On the day wu-xu, the Ministry submitted: "In recent times in selecting women for the inner quarters, some come from humble families with no training in ritual or instruction;

sentences.zh: 或刑戮之家，憂怨所積。

translations.literal: some come from families punished by law, with accumulated grief and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: some come from families punished by law, with accumulated grief and resentment.

sentences.zh: 請自今後宮及東宮內職有闕，皆選良家有才行者充，以禮聘納；

translations.literal: We request that henceforth whenever there are vacancies in the rear palace or inner offices of the Eastern Palace, only women of good families with virtue and ability be chosen, brought in through proper betrothal and reception;
translations.idiomatic: We request that henceforth whenever there are vacancies in the rear palace or inner offices of the Eastern Palace, only women of good families with virtue and ability be chosen and brought in through proper betrothal and reception;

sentences.zh: 其沒官口及素微賤之人，皆不得補用。」

translations.literal: those of confiscated households and those of long-standing humble status may none of them be appointed."
translations.idiomatic: those of confiscated households and those of long-standing humble status may none of them be appointed."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 上既詔宗室群臣襲封刺史，左庶子於志寧以為古今事殊，恐非久安之道，上疏爭之。

translations.literal: After the emperor had issued an edict that imperial clansmen and ministers should inherit appointments as regional inspectors, Left Pillar of the Crown Prince Yu Zhining held that past and present differed in circumstance and feared this was not a path to lasting peace; he submitted a memorial disputing it.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor had issued an edict that imperial clansmen and ministers should inherit appointments as regional inspectors, Left Pillar of the Crown Prince Yu Zhining held that past and present differed in circumstance and feared this was not a path to lasting peace; he submitted a memorial disputing it.

sentences.zh: 侍御史馬周亦上疏，以為：「堯、舜之父，猶有朱、均之子。

translations.literal: Censor Ma Zhou also submitted a memorial, holding: "Even the fathers of Yao and Shun had sons like Danzhu and Shangjun.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Ma Zhou also submitted a memorial, holding: "Even the fathers of Yao and Shun had sons like Danzhu and Shangjun.

sentences.zh: 倘有孩童嗣職，萬一驕愚，兆庶被其殃而國家受其敗。

translations.literal: If a child succeeds to office, should he by any chance prove arrogant and foolish, the myriad people would suffer calamity and the state would suffer ruin.
translations.idiomatic: If a child succeeds to office and by any chance proves arrogant and foolish, the myriad people would suffer calamity and the state would suffer ruin.

sentences.zh: 正欲絕之也，則子文之治猶在；

translations.literal: If one wished to cut off inheritance, Ziwen's good governance would still remain;
translations.idiomatic: If one wished to cut off inheritance, Ziwen's good governance would still remain;

sentences.zh: 正欲留之也，而欒黶之惡已彰。

translations.literal: if one wished to preserve it, Luan Yan's wickedness was already manifest.
translations.idiomatic: if one wished to preserve it, Luan Yan's wickedness was already manifest.

sentences.zh: 與其毒害於見存之百姓，則寧使割恩於已亡之一臣，明矣。

translations.literal: Rather than poison the living common people, it is better to sever favor toward one minister already dead—the point is clear.
translations.idiomatic: Rather than poison the living common people, it is better to sever favor toward one minister already dead—the point is clear.

sentences.zh: 然則向所謂愛之者，乃適所以傷之也。

translations.literal: Thus what was called loving them is precisely what harms them.
translations.idiomatic: Thus what was called loving them is precisely what harms them.

sentences.zh: 臣謂宜賦以茅土，疇其戶邑，必有材行，隨器授官，使其人得奉大恩而子孫終其福祿。」

translations.literal: Your subject holds that they should be granted fief lands and allotted households; only when there is talent and conduct should office be conferred according to capacity, so that the man may receive great favor and his descendants may enjoy their blessings and emoluments to the end."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject holds that they should be granted fief lands and allotted households; only when there is talent and conduct should office be conferred according to capacity, so that the man may receive great favor and his descendants may enjoy their blessings and emoluments to the end."

sentences.zh: 會司空、趙州刺史長孫無忌等皆不願之國，上表固讓，稱：「承恩以來，形影相吊，若履春冰；

translations.literal: Meanwhile, Minister of Works and regional inspector of Zhaozhou Zhangsun Wuji and others all wished not to go to their assigned prefectures; they submitted memorials firmly declining, stating: "Since receiving this grace, we have been like shadow mourning form, as if treading spring ice;
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile, Minister of Works and regional inspector of Zhaozhou Zhangsun Wuji and others all wished not to go to their assigned prefectures. They submitted memorials firmly declining, stating: "Since receiving this grace, we have been like shadow mourning form, as if treading spring ice;

sentences.zh: 宗戚憂虞，如置湯火。

translations.literal: kinsmen and relatives are filled with worry and dread, as if placed in boiling water or fire.
translations.idiomatic: Our kinsmen and relatives are filled with worry and dread, as if placed in boiling water or fire.

sentences.zh: 緬惟三代封建，蓋由力不能制，因而利之，禮樂節文，多非己出。

translations.literal: Reflecting on the feudal enfeoffment of the Three Dynasties, it was largely because the central power could not control the regions and so turned the situation to advantage; ritual, music, and ceremonial forms were mostly not of their own making.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on the feudal enfeoffment of the Three Dynasties, it was largely because the central power could not control the regions and so turned the situation to advantage. Ritual, music, and ceremonial forms were mostly not of their own making.

sentences.zh: 兩漢罷侯置守，蠲除曩弊，深協事宜，今因臣等，復有變更，恐紊聖朝綱紀；

translations.literal: The two Han dynasties abolished feudal lords and installed regional inspectors, removing old abuses—this accorded deeply with the needs of the times. Now on account of us ministers there is again to be change, and we fear disorder in the sacred court's order;
translations.idiomatic: The two Han dynasties abolished feudal lords and installed regional inspectors, removing old abuses—this accorded deeply with the needs of the times. Now on account of us ministers there is again to be change, and we fear disorder in the sacred court's order;

sentences.zh: 且後世愚幼不肖之嗣，或抵冒邦憲，自取誅夷，更因延世之賞，致成剿絕之禍，良可哀愍。

translations.literal: moreover, foolish, young, or unworthy successors in later generations may violate the laws of the state and bring execution upon themselves; to extend hereditary rewards would only bring about the calamity of extermination—this is truly pitiable.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, foolish, young, or unworthy successors in later generations may violate the laws of the state and bring execution upon themselves. To extend hereditary rewards would only bring about the calamity of extermination—this is truly pitiable.

sentences.zh: 願停渙汗之旨，賜其性命之恩。」

translations.literal: We beg that the edict of sweeping grace be halted and the favor of sparing our lives be granted."
translations.idiomatic: We beg that the edict of sweeping grace be halted and the favor of sparing our lives be granted."

sentences.zh: 無忌又因子婦長樂公主固請於上，且言：「臣披荊棘事陛下，今海內寧一，奈何棄之外州，與遷徙何異！」

translations.literal: Wuji also, through his daughter-in-law Princess Changle, pressed a firm plea to the emperor, saying further: "Your subject cleared thorns to serve Your Majesty; now the realm within the seas is at peace—why cast us off to outer prefectures, no different from exile!"
translations.idiomatic: Wuji also, through his daughter-in-law Princess Changle, pressed a firm plea to the emperor, saying further: "Your subject cleared thorns to serve Your Majesty; now the realm within the seas is at peace—why cast us off to outer prefectures, no different from exile!"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「割地以封功臣，古今通義，意欲公之後嗣，輔朕子孫，共傳永久；

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Granting land to enfeoff meritorious ministers is the common principle of past and present. My intent is that your descendants may assist my children and grandchildren and jointly preserve the realm for ages;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Granting land to enfeoff meritorious ministers is the common principle of past and present. My intent is that your descendants may assist my children and grandchildren and jointly preserve the realm for ages;

sentences.zh: 而公等乃復發言怨望，朕豈強公等以茅土邪！」

translations.literal: yet you again speak words of resentment and discontent—do I force you to accept fief lands!"
translations.idiomatic: yet you again speak words of resentment and discontent—do I force you to accept fief lands!"

sentences.zh: 庚子，詔停世封刺史。

translations.literal: On the day geng-zi, an edict halted hereditary appointment as regional inspectors.
translations.idiomatic: On the day geng-zi, an edict halted hereditary appointment as regional inspectors.

sentences.zh: 高昌王麴文泰多遏絕西域朝貢，伊吾先臣西突厥，既而內屬，文泰與西突厥共擊之。

translations.literal: King Qu Wentai of Gaochang frequently blocked and cut off tribute missions from the Western Regions. Yiwu had first submitted to the Western Turks, then turned inward to our allegiance; Wentai joined with the Western Turks to attack it.
translations.idiomatic: King Qu Wentai of Gaochang frequently blocked and cut off tribute missions from the Western Regions. Yiwu had first submitted to the Western Turks, then turned inward to our allegiance; Wentai joined with the Western Turks to attack it.

sentences.zh: 上下書切責，征其大臣阿史那矩，欲與議事，文泰不遣，遣其長史麴雍來謝罪。

translations.literal: The emperor sent letters of stern reproof, summoning his minister Ashina Ju to discuss affairs; Wentai did not send him but dispatched his chief administrator Qu Yong to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent letters of stern reproof, summoning his minister Ashina Ju to discuss affairs. Wentai did not send him but dispatched his chief administrator Qu Yong to apologize.

sentences.zh: 頡利之亡也，中國人在突厥者或奔高昌，詔文泰歸之，文泰蔽匿不遣。

translations.literal: When Jiali perished, Chinese subjects who had been among the Turks fled some to Gaochang; an edict ordered Wentai to return them, but Wentai concealed them and did not send them back.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiali perished, some Chinese subjects who had been among the Turks fled to Gaochang. An edict ordered Wentai to return them, but Wentai concealed them and did not send them back.

sentences.zh: 又與西突厥共擊破焉耆，焉耆訴之。

translations.literal: He again joined the Western Turks in attacking and defeating Yanqi; Yanqi lodged a complaint.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined the Western Turks in attacking and defeating Yanqi; Yanqi lodged a complaint.

sentences.zh: 上遣虞部郎中李道裕往問狀，且謂其使者曰：「高昌數年以來，朝貢脫略，無籓臣禮，所置官號，皆准天朝，築城掘溝，預備攻討。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched Li Daoyu of the Ministry of Works to investigate, and also said to Gaochang's envoy: "In recent years Gaochang has neglected tribute and owed the courtesies due a vassal; the official titles it has established all mirror the heavenly court; it has built walls and dug moats in preparation for attack.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched Li Daoyu of the Ministry of Works to investigate, and also said to Gaochang's envoy: "In recent years Gaochang has neglected tribute and owed the courtesies due a vassal. The official titles it has established all mirror the heavenly court. It has built walls and dug moats in preparation for attack.

sentences.zh: 我使者至彼，文泰語之云：『鷹飛於天，雉伏於蒿，貓游於堂，鼠□於穴，各得其所，豈不能自生邪！』

translations.literal: When our envoy arrived there, Wentai told him: 'The hawk flies in the sky, the pheasant crouches in the grass, the cat roams the hall, mice hide in their holes—each finds its place; cannot we likewise live in peace?'
translations.idiomatic: When our envoy arrived there, Wentai told him: 'The hawk flies in the sky, the pheasant crouches in the grass, the cat roams the hall, mice hide in their holes—each finds its place; cannot we likewise live in peace?'

sentences.zh: 又遣使謂薛延陀云：『既為可汗，則與天子匹敵，何為拜其使者！』

translations.literal: He also sent an envoy to tell the Xueyantuo: 'Since you are khan, you are the emperor's equal—why bow to his envoy!'
translations.idiomatic: He also sent an envoy to tell the Xueyantuo: 'Since you are khan, you are the emperor's equal—why bow to his envoy!'

sentences.zh: 事人無禮，又間鄰國，為惡不誅，善何以勸！

translations.literal: To treat others without courtesy, and moreover to sow discord among neighboring states—if wickedness goes unpunished, how can goodness be encouraged!
translations.idiomatic: To treat others without courtesy, and moreover to sow discord among neighboring states—if wickedness goes unpunished, how can goodness be encouraged!

sentences.zh: 明年當發兵擊汝。」

translations.literal: Next year troops will be sent to attack you."
translations.idiomatic: Next year troops will be sent to attack you."

sentences.zh: 三月，薛延陀可汗遣使上言：「奴受恩思報，請發所部為軍導以擊高昌。」

translations.literal: In the third month, the Xueyantuo khan sent envoys to submit: "Your servant, having received grace, seeks to repay it; I request to mobilize my tribes as military guides to attack Gaochang."
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, the Xueyantuo khan sent envoys to submit: "Your servant, having received grace, seeks to repay it. I request to mobilize my tribes as military guides to attack Gaochang."

sentences.zh: 上遣民部尚書唐儉、右領軍大將軍執失思力繼繒帛賜薛延陀，與謀進取。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched Minister of the Household Tang Jian and Right General of the Rear Guard Zhishi Sili with silks and cloth to bestow on the Xueyantuo, and consulted on the plan of attack.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched Minister of the Household Tang Jian and Right General of the Rear Guard Zhishi Sili with silks and cloth to bestow on the Xueyantuo, and consulted on the plan of attack.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，戊寅，上幸九成宮。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day wu-yin, the emperor visited Jiucheng Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the day wu-yin, the emperor visited Jiucheng Palace.

sentences.zh: 初，突厥突利可汗之弟結社率從突利入朝，歷位中郎將。

translations.literal: Previously, Jieshelü, younger brother of the Turkic khagan Tuli, had followed Tuli in coming to court and had risen to the rank of palace guard captain.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, Jieshelü, younger brother of the Turkic khagan Tuli, had followed Tuli in coming to court and had risen to the rank of palace guard captain.

sentences.zh: 居家無賴，怨突利斥之，乃誣告其謀反，上由是薄之，久不進秩。

translations.literal: At home he was dissolute; resenting Tuli for dismissing him, he falsely accused him of plotting rebellion; the emperor therefore thought little of him and for a long time did not advance his rank.
translations.idiomatic: At home he was dissolute. Resenting Tuli for dismissing him, he falsely accused him of plotting rebellion. The emperor therefore thought little of him and for a long time did not advance his rank.

sentences.zh: 結社率陰結故部落，得四十餘人，謀因晉王治四鼓出宮，開門辟仗，馳入宮門，直指御帳，可有大功。

translations.literal: Jieshelü secretly rallied his former tribesmen, gathering more than forty men, and plotted that when Prince Jin Zhi left the palace at the fourth watch they would open the gate, distribute weapons, gallop through the palace gate, and charge straight at the imperial tent—there great merit could be won.
translations.idiomatic: Jieshelü secretly rallied his former tribesmen, gathering more than forty men, and plotted that when Prince Jin Zhi left the palace at the fourth watch they would open the gate, distribute weapons, gallop through the palace gate, and charge straight at the imperial tent—there great merit could be won.

sentences.zh: 甲申，擁突利之子賀邏鶻夜伏於宮外，會大風，晉王未出，結社率恐曉，遂犯行宮，逾四重幕，弓矢亂髮，衛士死者數十人。

translations.literal: On the day jia-shen, he took Tuli's son Heluoge and lay in ambush outside the palace by night; a great wind arose, Prince Jin did not emerge, and fearing dawn Jieshelü attacked the temporary palace, passed through four layers of screens, arrows flying in disorder; several dozen guards were killed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jia-shen, he took Tuli's son Heluoge and lay in ambush outside the palace by night. A great wind arose, Prince Jin did not emerge, and fearing dawn Jieshelü attacked the temporary palace. He passed through four layers of screens with arrows flying in disorder; several dozen guards were killed.

sentences.zh: 折衝孫武開等帥眾奮擊，久之，乃退，馳入御廄，盜馬二十餘匹，北走，度渭，欲奔其部落，追獲，斬之，原賀邏鶻投於嶺表。

translations.literal: Palace Guard Commander Sun Wukai and others led troops in fierce counterattack; after a long time they withdrew, galloped into the imperial stables, stole more than twenty horses, fled north, crossed the Wei River, and sought to reach their tribesmen; they were pursued and captured; Jieshelü was beheaded, and Heluoge was pardoned and sent beyond the mountain passes.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Guard Commander Sun Wukai and others led troops in fierce counterattack. After a long time the assailants withdrew, galloped into the imperial stables, stole more than twenty horses, fled north, crossed the Wei River, and sought to reach their tribesmen. They were pursued and captured; Jieshelü was beheaded, and Heluoge was pardoned and sent beyond the mountain passes.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，遣武候將軍上官懷仁擊巴、壁、洋、集四州反獠，平之，虜男女六千餘口。

translations.literal: On the day geng-yin, Martial Guard General Shangguan Huairen was dispatched to attack the rebel Liao of the four prefectures Ba, Bi, Yang, and Ji; he pacified them and captured more than six thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: On the day geng-yin, Martial Guard General Shangguan Huairen was dispatched to attack the rebel Liao of the four prefectures Ba, Bi, Yang, and Ji. He pacified them and captured more than six thousand men and women.

sentences.zh: 五月，旱。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, there was drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, there was drought.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，詔五品以上上封事。

translations.literal: On the day jia-yin, an edict ordered officials of fifth rank and above to submit sealed memorials.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jia-yin, an edict ordered officials of fifth rank and above to submit sealed memorials.

sentences.zh: 魏徵上疏，以為：「陛下志業，比貞觀之初，漸不克終者凡十條。」

translations.literal: Wei Zheng submitted a memorial, holding: "Your Majesty's resolve and enterprise, compared with the beginning of the Zhenguan era, has gradually failed to reach completion in ten respects."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng submitted a memorial, holding: "Your Majesty's resolve and enterprise, compared with the beginning of the Zhenguan era, has gradually failed to reach completion in ten respects."

sentences.zh: 其間一條以為：「頃年以來，輕用民力。

translations.literal: Among them one item held: "In recent years the people's labor has been lightly expended.
translations.idiomatic: Among them one item held: "In recent years the people's labor has been lightly expended.

sentences.zh: 乃云：『百姓無事則驕逸，勞役則易使。』

translations.literal: It is even said: 'When the common people have nothing to do they grow arrogant and slack; when put to labor they are easy to command.'
translations.idiomatic: It is even said: 'When the common people have nothing to do they grow arrogant and slack; when put to labor they are easy to command.'

sentences.zh: 自古未有因百姓逸而敗、勞而安者也。

translations.literal: From ancient times there has never been a case where the state fell because the common people had leisure, or was secure because they labored.
translations.idiomatic: There has never been a dynasty that fell because its people had too much leisure, or found stability because they were kept overworked.

sentences.zh: 此恐非興邦之至言。」

translations.literal: This fearfully is not supreme speech for raising a state."
translations.idiomatic: I suspect this is hardly the surest counsel for building a flourishing realm."

sentences.zh: 上深加獎歎，云：「已列諸屏障，朝夕瞻仰，並錄付史官。」

translations.literal: The emperor deeply added praise and sighs, saying: "Already displayed among the screens, morning and evening gazed upon in reverence, and also recorded and entrusted to the historians."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him warmly and exclaimed: "I have hung it among my screens to read morning and evening, and I shall also have it copied for the court historians."

sentences.zh: 仍賜征黃金十斤。

translations.literal: He still bestowed on Zheng ten jin of gold.
translations.idiomatic: He also awarded Wei Zheng ten jin of gold.

sentences.zh: 廄馬二匹。

translations.literal: Two horses from the stable.
translations.idiomatic: He also gave him two horses from the imperial stables.

sentences.zh: 六月，渝州人侯弘仁自牂柯開道，經西趙，出邕州，以通交、桂，蠻、俚降者二萬八千餘戶。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Hou Hongren of Yuzhou, starting from Zangke, opened a road, passing through Xizhao, exiting at Yongzhou, to connect Jiao and Gui; Man and Li who submitted numbered more than twenty-eight thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Hou Hongren of Yuzhou opened a route from Zangke through Xizhao to Yongzhou, linking Jiaozhi and Guizhou. More than twenty-eight thousand Man and Li households submitted.

sentences.zh: 丙申，立皇弟元嬰為滕王。

translations.literal: On the day bing-shen, the emperor's younger brother Yuanying was established as Prince of Teng.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bing-shen, the emperor's younger brother Li Yuanying was created Prince of Teng.

sentences.zh: 自結社率之反，言事者多雲突厥留河南不便，秋，七月，庚戌，詔右武候大將軍、化州都督、懷化郡王李思摩為乙彌泥孰俟利苾可汗，賜之鼓纛；

translations.literal: Since the rebellion of Jiesheshuai, those who spoke on affairs mostly said that keeping the Turks south of the river was inconvenient. In autumn, the seventh month, on the day geng-xu, an edict made Right Martial Guard General, Protector-General of Huazhou, Prince of Huaihua Commandery Li Simo the Yiminishijilibi Qaghan, and bestowed upon him drums and banners;
translations.idiomatic: Ever since Jiesheshuai's revolt, memorialists had repeatedly argued that keeping Turks south of the Yellow River was unwise. In autumn, the seventh month, on the day geng-xu, an edict named Right Martial Guard General Li Simo, Protector-General of Huazhou and Prince of Huaihua Commandery, as Qaghan Yiminishijilibi, and granted him drums and standards of command;

sentences.zh: 突厥及胡在諸州安置者，並令渡河，還其舊部，俾世作籓屏，長保邊塞。

translations.literal: Turks and Hu settled in the various prefectures were all ordered to cross the river, return to their old tribes, be made to serve generation after generation as border screens, and long preserve the frontier passes.
translations.idiomatic: All Turks and other nomadic peoples settled in the prefectures were ordered to cross the river, return to their former lands, and serve for generations as a bulwark of the frontier.

sentences.zh: 突厥鹹憚薛延陀，不肯出塞。

translations.literal: The Turks all feared Xueyantuo and were unwilling to go beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks feared Xueyantuo and refused to leave the frontier zone.

sentences.zh: 上遣司農卿郭嗣本賜薛延陀璽書，言「頡利既敗，其部落鹹來歸化，我略其舊過，嘉其後善，待其達官皆如吾百寮、部落皆如吾百姓。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Minister of Revenue Guo Siben to bestow upon Xueyantuo an imperial letter, saying: "Since Jieli was defeated, his tribes have all come to submit. I overlook their old offenses, commend their later virtue, and treat their high officials like my hundred officials and their tribes like my common people.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Minister of Revenue Guo Siben to deliver an imperial letter to Xueyantuo stating: "After Jieli's defeat, his people have all submitted. I forgive their past wrongs and honor their present reform. I treat their chiefs as I do my own court officials, and their tribes as my own subjects.

sentences.zh: 中國貴尚禮義，不滅人國，前破突厥，止為頡利一人為百姓害，實不貪其土地，利其人畜，恆欲更立可汗，故置所降部落於河南，任其畜牧。

translations.literal: China esteems and honors ritual and righteousness, and does not destroy other states. When we previously defeated the Turks, it was only because Jieli alone harmed the people. We truly did not covet their land or desire their people and livestock. We always wished to establish another qaghan, and therefore placed the submitted tribes south of the river and allowed them to graze their herds.
translations.idiomatic: The Middle Kingdom values ritual and righteousness and does not annihilate other peoples. Our earlier defeat of the Turks was aimed only at Jieli, who had harmed the people — not at seizing their lands or livestock. We always intended to establish a new qaghan, which is why we settled the surrendered tribes south of the river and let them pasture their herds.

sentences.zh: 今戶口蕃滋，吾心甚喜。

translations.literal: Now households and population flourish and multiply — my heart is greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Now that their numbers have multiplied, I am greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 既許立之，不可失信。

translations.literal: Having already promised to establish him, one cannot break faith.
translations.idiomatic: Since I have promised to install him, I cannot go back on my word.

sentences.zh: 秋中將遣突厥渡河，復其故國。

translations.literal: In mid-autumn I shall send the Turks across the river to restore their former state.
translations.idiomatic: In mid-autumn I shall send the Turks back across the river to restore their homeland.

sentences.zh: 爾薛延陀受冊在前，突厥受冊在後，後者為小，前者為大。

translations.literal: You Xueyantuo received investiture first; the Turks received investiture later — the latter is the lesser, the former is the greater.
translations.idiomatic: You Xueyantuo were invested first and the Turks second. The one invested later ranks below; the one invested earlier ranks above.

sentences.zh: 爾在磧北，突厥在磧南，各守土疆，鎮撫部落。

translations.literal: You are north of the desert; the Turks are south of the desert. Each guard your territories and pacify your tribes.
translations.idiomatic: You shall remain north of the desert and the Turks south of it, each holding your own territory and keeping your tribes in order.

sentences.zh: 其逾分故相抄掠，我則發兵，各問其罪。」

translations.literal: If they overstep bounds and deliberately raid each other, I shall dispatch troops and hold each accountable for his offense."
translations.idiomatic: If either side oversteps its bounds and raids the other, I shall send troops and punish whichever side is at fault."

sentences.zh: 薛延陀奉詔。

translations.literal: Xueyantuo received the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Xueyantuo accepted the edict.

sentences.zh: 於是遣思摩帥所部建牙於河北，上御齊政殿餞之，思摩涕泣，奉觴上壽曰：「奴等破亡之餘，分為灰壤，陛下存其骸骨，復立為可汗，願萬世子孫恆事陛下。」

translations.literal: Thereupon Simo was sent to lead his followers and establish his headquarters north of the river. The emperor went to Qizheng Hall to give him a farewell feast. Simo wept, raised a cup to wish the emperor long life, and said: "We slaves, the remnant of a shattered people, scattered as dust and ashes — Your Majesty preserved our bones and reestablished us as qaghan. May our descendants for ten thousand generations forever serve Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Simo was then sent to lead his people and establish his court north of the river. The emperor went to Qizheng Hall to bid him farewell. Simo wept, raised his cup in toast, and said: "We are the shattered remnants of a broken people, scattered to dust. Your Majesty has spared our bones and restored us as qaghan. May our descendants serve you for ten thousand generations."

sentences.zh: 又遣禮部尚書趙郡王孝恭等繼冊書，就其種落，築壇於河上而立之。

translations.literal: He also sent Minister of Rites, Prince of Zhao Commandery Li Xiaogong, and others to follow with the investiture documents, and at their tribal settlement built an altar on the riverbank to install him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also dispatched Minister of Rites Li Xiaogong, Prince of Zhao Commandery, and others with investiture documents to raise an altar on the riverbank and formally install him among his people.

sentences.zh: 上謂侍臣曰：「中國，根幹也；

translations.literal: The emperor said to his attending officials: "China is the root and trunk;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his attendants: "The Middle Kingdom is the root and trunk;

sentences.zh: 四夷，枝葉也；

translations.literal: The four barbarians are the branches and leaves;
translations.idiomatic: the four quarters of the frontier are the branches and leaves;

sentences.zh: 割根幹以奉枝葉，木安得滋榮！

translations.literal: Cut the root and trunk to serve the branches and leaves — how can the tree flourish!
translations.idiomatic: If you cut away the root to nourish the branches, how can the tree ever thrive?

sentences.zh: 朕不用魏徵言，幾致狼狽。」

translations.literal: If I had not used Wei Zheng's words, I would nearly have been brought to disgrace."
translations.idiomatic: Had I not heeded Wei Zheng, I would nearly have brought disaster upon myself."

sentences.zh: 又以左屯衛將軍阿史那忠為左賢王，左武衛將軍阿史那泥熟為右賢王。

translations.literal: He also made Left Garrison Guard General Ashina Zhong Left Wise Prince, and Left Martial Guard General Ashina Nishu Right Wise Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He also appointed Left Garrison Guard General Ashina Zhong Left Wise Prince and Left Martial Guard General Ashina Nishu Right Wise Prince.

sentences.zh: 忠，蘇尼失之子也，上遇之甚厚，妻以宗女；

translations.literal: Zhong was the son of Sunishi. The emperor treated him with great favor and gave him an imperial clanswoman in marriage;
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was the son of Sunishi. The emperor favored him greatly and gave him an imperial princess in marriage;

sentences.zh: 及出塞，懷慕中國，見使者必泣涕請入侍；

translations.literal: When he went beyond the passes, he longed for China; whenever he saw envoys he wept and begged to enter and serve at court;
translations.idiomatic: Once he crossed the frontier, he longed for the capital; whenever he met imperial envoys he wept and pleaded to be allowed to serve at court;

sentences.zh: 詔許之。

translations.literal: An edict granted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 八月，辛未朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the first day of the cycle xin-wei, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the first day xin-wei, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 詔以「身體髮膚，不敢毀傷。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "The body, hair, and skin — one dares not harm them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "The body, hair, and skin received from one's parents must not be deliberately harmed.

sentences.zh: 比來訴訟者或自毀耳目，自今有犯，先笞四十，然後依法。」

translations.literal: Recently litigants have sometimes destroyed their own ears and eyes. From now on, if there is an offense, first flog forty strokes, then proceed according to law."
translations.idiomatic: Lately some plaintiffs have mutilated their own ears or eyes to bolster their cases. Henceforth offenders shall first receive forty strokes of the rod and then be judged under the usual statutes."

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲申，車駕還京師。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day jia-shen, the imperial carriage returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the day jia-shen, the emperor returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十一月，辛亥，以侍中楊師道為中書令。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day xin-hai, Attendant-in-Ordinary Yang Shidao was made Chief of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the day xin-hai, Attendant-in-Ordinary Yang Shidao was appointed Chief of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，尚書左丞劉洎為黃門侍郎、參知政事。

translations.literal: On the day wu-chen, Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs Liu Ji was made Vice Director of the Yellow Gate and made privy to state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wu-chen, Left Assistant Director Liu Ji was made Vice Director of the Yellow Gate and given a role in deliberating on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 上猶冀高昌王文泰悔過，復下璽書，示以禍福，征之入朝；

translations.literal: The emperor still hoped that Gaochang King Wenkai would repent; he again issued an imperial letter, showing fortune and disaster, and summoned him to court;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still hoped King Wenkai of Gaochang would repent. He sent another imperial letter, setting out the rewards of submission and the costs of defiance, and summoned him to court;

sentences.zh: 文泰竟稱疾不至。

translations.literal: Wenkai ultimately pleaded illness and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Wenkai claimed illness and refused to come.

sentences.zh: 十二月，壬申，遣交河行軍大總管、吏部尚書侯君集，副總管兼左屯衛大將軍薛萬均等將兵擊之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day ren-shen, he dispatched Campaign Commander-in-Chief of Jiaohe, Minister of Personnel Hou Junji, Deputy Commander and Left Garrison Guard General Xue Wanjun, and others to lead troops and attack him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day ren-shen, he dispatched Hou Junji, Minister of Personnel and overall commander of the Jiaohe campaign, and his deputy Xue Wanjun, Left Garrison Guard General, with an army to attack Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，立皇子福為趙王。

translations.literal: On the day yi-hai, the imperial son Fu was established as Prince of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yi-hai, the emperor's son Li Fu was created Prince of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 己丑，吐谷渾王諾曷缽來朝，以宗女為弘化公主，妻之。

translations.literal: On the day ji-chou, Tuyuhun King Nuohebo came to court; an imperial clanswoman was made Princess Honghua and given to him in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: On the day ji-chou, King Nuohebo of Tuyuhun came to court. An imperial clanswoman was created Princess Honghua and given to him in marriage.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，上畋於咸陽，癸巳，還宮。

translations.literal: On the day ren-chen, the emperor hunted at Xianyang; on the day gui-si, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the day ren-chen the emperor hunted at Xianyang; on the day gui-si he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 太子承乾頗以游畋廢學，右庶子張玄素諫，不聽。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Chengqian greatly neglected study for excursions and hunting. Right Companion Zhang Xuansu remonstrated, but the prince would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Chengqian neglected his studies in favor of hunting and outings. Right Companion Zhang Xuansu remonstrated with him, but the prince paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 是歲，天下州府凡三百五十八，縣一千五百一十一。

translations.literal: That year, throughout the realm there were in all three hundred fifty-eight prefectures and counties, and one thousand five hundred eleven districts.
translations.idiomatic: That year the empire comprised three hundred fifty-eight prefectures and one thousand five hundred eleven counties.

sentences.zh: 太史令傅奕精究術數之書，而終不之信，遇病，不呼醫餌藥。

translations.literal: Grand Astrologer Fu Yi deeply investigated books of numerology and the occult, yet ultimately did not believe in them. When he fell ill, he did not summon physicians or take medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Astrologer Fu Yi had mastered the texts of numerology and divination, yet refused to believe in them. When he fell ill he would neither call a physician nor take medicine.

sentences.zh: 有僧自西域來，善咒術，能令人立死，復咒之使蘇。

translations.literal: There was a monk from the Western Regions skilled in incantations who could make a person die on the spot and then revive him with another incantation.
translations.idiomatic: A monk from the Western Regions arrived, skilled in spell-craft: he could kill a man instantly, then bring him back to life with another spell.

sentences.zh: 上擇飛騎中壯者試之，皆如其言；

translations.literal: The emperor selected robust men from the Flying Cavalry to test him — all happened as he said;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor chose sturdy men from the Flying Cavalry to test the claim, and each trial unfolded exactly as the monk had promised;

sentences.zh: 以告奕，奕曰：「此邪術也。

translations.literal: This was reported to Yi. Yi said: "This is evil sorcery.
translations.idiomatic: When this was reported to Fu Yi, he said: "This is black magic.

sentences.zh: 臣聞邪不干正，請使咒臣，必不能行。」

translations.literal: I have heard that evil does not overcome righteousness. Please have him curse me — it surely will not succeed."
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that evil cannot prevail over righteousness. Have him try his spell on me — it will fail."

sentences.zh: 上命僧咒奕，奕初無所覺，須臾，僧忽僵仆，若為物所擊，遂不復甦。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the monk to curse Yi. At first Yi felt nothing; presently the monk suddenly collapsed stiff, as if struck by something, and never revived again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the monk to curse Fu Yi. At first Yi felt nothing; then the monk suddenly collapsed as if struck down and never rose again.

sentences.zh: 又有婆羅門僧，言得佛齒，所擊前無堅物。

translations.literal: There was also a Brahman monk who claimed to possess a Buddha's tooth that would shatter anything hard placed before it when struck.
translations.idiomatic: Another Brahman monk claimed to possess a Buddha's tooth that, when struck against any hard object, would shatter what lay before it.

sentences.zh: 長安士女輻湊如市。

translations.literal: The gentlemen and ladies of Chang'an crowded in like a market.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Chang'an thronged to see it as densely as a marketplace.

sentences.zh: 奕時臥疾，謂其子曰：「吾聞有金剛石者，性至堅，物莫能傷，唯羚羊角能破之，汝往試焉。」

translations.literal: Yi was then bedridden with illness. He said to his son: "I have heard there is a substance called diamond whose nature is extremely hard — nothing can harm it; only antelope horn can break it. Go and test this."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yi lay ill at the time. He told his son: "I have heard that diamond is the hardest of substances and cannot be scratched by anything — except antelope horn. Go and test the tooth with horn."

sentences.zh: 其子往見佛齒，出角叩之，應手而碎，觀者乃止。

translations.literal: His son went to see the Buddha's tooth, produced horn and struck it — it shattered at once. The onlookers then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: His son went to the display, struck the tooth with antelope horn, and it shattered instantly. The crowd dispersed.

sentences.zh: 奕臨終，戒其子無得學佛書，時年八十五。

translations.literal: As Yi faced death, he admonished his son not to study Buddhist texts. He was eighty-five years old at the time.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Fu Yi forbade his son to study Buddhist scriptures. He was eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 又集魏、晉以來駁佛教者為《高識傳》十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: He also collected those who had refuted Buddhism from Wei and Jin down to his own time in ten scrolls of "Accounts of Higher Understanding," which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He had also compiled ten scrolls of anti-Buddhist writings from Wei and Jin times onward, titled Accounts of Higher Understanding, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 西突厥咥利失可汗之臣俟利發與乙毘咄陸可汗通謀作亂，咥利失窮蹙，逃奔鏺汗而死。

translations.literal: A minister of the Western Türk Qaghan Dilishi, Yiliba, colluded with Qaghan Yipiduolu to rebel. Dilishi, hard pressed, fled to Bohan and died there.
translations.idiomatic: Yiliba, a minister of the Western Türk qaghan Dilishi, conspired with Qaghan Yipiduolu to revolt. Dilishi, driven to desperation, fled to Bohan and died there.

sentences.zh: 弩失畢部落迎其弟子薄布特勒立之，是為乙毘沙缽羅葉護可汗。

translations.literal: The Nushibi tribes welcomed his nephew Bo Botele and established him — this was Qaghan Yipishaboheluoyehu.
translations.idiomatic: The Nushibi tribes installed his nephew Bo Botele as qaghan — Qaghan Yipishaboheluoyehu.

sentences.zh: 沙缽羅葉護既立，建庭於雖合水北，謂之南庭，自龜茲、鄯善、且末、吐火羅、焉耆、石、史、何、穆、康等國皆附之。

translations.literal: Once Shaboheluoyehu was established, he set up his court north of the Suihe River, calling it the Southern Court. From Kucha, Shanshan, Qiemo, Tuhuoluo, Yanqi, Shi, Shiji, He, Mu, Kang, and other states — all submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Once installed, Shaboheluoyehu established his court north of the Suihe River — the Southern Court. Kucha, Shanshan, Qiemo, Tuhuoluo, Yanqi, and the kingdoms of Shi, Shiji, He, Mu, Kang, and others all submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 咄陸建牙於鏃曷山西，謂之北庭，自厥越失、拔悉彌、駁馬、結骨、火燖、觸水昆等國皆附之，以伊列水為境。

translations.literal: Duolu established his headquarters west of Zuogeshan, calling it the Northern Court. From Jueyueshi, Basmil, Boma, Jiegu, Huoxun, Chushuikun, and other states — all submitted to him, with the Yilie River as boundary.
translations.idiomatic: Duolu established his court west of Zuogeshan — the Northern Court. Jueyueshi, Basmil, Boma, Jiegu, Huoxun, Chushuikun, and other peoples submitted to him, with the Yilie River as the boundary between them.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲寅，上幸魏王泰第，赦雍州長安系囚大辟以下，免延康裡今年租賦，賜泰府僚屬及同裡老人有差。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day jia-yin, the emperor visited the residence of Prince of Wei Tai. He pardoned prisoners of Yongzhou and Chang'an down from capital offenses, exempted Yan'kang Ward from this year's taxes and levies, and bestowed gifts in varying measure on Tai's staff and the elders of the same ward.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the day jia-yin, the emperor visited Prince of Wei Li Tai's residence. He pardoned Chang'an prisoners sentenced below capital crimes, remitted this year's taxes for Yan'kang Ward, and gave presents in varying amounts to Tai's household staff and elderly neighbors.

sentences.zh: 二月，丁丑，上幸國子監，觀釋奠，命祭酒孔穎達講《孝經》，賜祭酒以下至諸生高第帛有差。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day ding-chou, the emperor visited the Directorate of Education, observed the Sacrifice to Confucius, ordered Libationer Kong Yingda to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety, and bestowed silk in varying measure on the libationer down to students of highest rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day ding-chou, the emperor visited the Imperial Academy for the Confucian sacrifice. He had Libationer Kong Yingda expound the Classic of Filial Piety and awarded silk in graded amounts to Kong and the highest-ranked students.

sentences.zh: 是時上大征天下名儒為學官，數幸國子監，使之講論，學生能明一大經已上皆得補官。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor greatly summoned famous Confucians throughout the realm as academy officers. He repeatedly visited the Directorate of Education, had them lecture and debate, and students who could master one major classic or more all received official appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had summoned renowned scholars from across the empire to serve as academy instructors. He visited the Imperial Academy repeatedly to hear them lecture and debate, and any student who mastered at least one of the major classics was eligible for office.

sentences.zh: 增築學舍千二百間，增學生滿三千二百六十員，自屯營飛騎，亦給博士，使授以經，有能通經者，聽得貢舉。

translations.literal: One thousand two hundred more lecture halls were built; students were increased to fill three thousand two hundred sixty places. Even from the garrison camps and Flying Cavalry, instructors were also provided to teach them the classics; those who could master the classics were permitted to take the civil service examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve hundred new rooms were added and enrollment raised to 3,260. Even garrison troops and Flying Cavalry were assigned instructors in the classics, and any who mastered a text were allowed to sit for the examinations.

sentences.zh: 於是四方學者雲集京師，乃至高麗、百濟、新羅、高昌、吐蕃諸酋長亦遣子弟請入國學，升講筵者至八千餘人。

translations.literal: Thereupon scholars from the four directions gathered like clouds in the capital. Even chieftains of Goguryeo, Baekje, Silla, Gaochang, and Tibet sent sons and younger brothers requesting entry into the National Academy. Those who ascended the lecture benches reached more than eight thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars from every quarter flocked to the capital. Even chieftains of Goguryeo, Baekje, Silla, Gaochang, and Tibet sent sons and younger kinsmen to enroll in the National Academy. More than eight thousand students attended the lectures.

sentences.zh: 上以師說多門，章句繁雜，命孔穎達與諸儒撰定《五經》疏，謂之《正義》，令學者習之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because teachers' doctrines were many-branched and chapter-and-sentence commentary was complex and tangled, ordered Kong Yingda and the Confucians to compile commentaries on the Five Classics, calling them "Correct Meanings," and commanded scholars to study them.
translations.idiomatic: Because competing schools had proliferated and commentaries had grown tangled, the emperor commissioned Kong Yingda and other scholars to compile authoritative commentaries on the Five Classics — the Correct Meanings — and ordered students to study them.

sentences.zh: 壬午，上幸驪山溫湯；

translations.literal: On the day ren-wu, the emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li;
translations.idiomatic: On the day ren-wu the emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li;

sentences.zh: 辛卯，還宮。

translations.literal: On the day xin-mao, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xin-mao he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 乙未，詔求近世名儒梁皇甫侃、褚仲都，周熊安生、沈重，陳沈文阿、周弘正、張譏，隋何妥、劉炫等子孫以聞，當加引擢。

translations.literal: On the day yi-wei, an edict sought the descendants of recent famous Confucians — Liang's Huangfu Kan and Chu Zhongdu, Zhou's Xiong Ansheng and Shen Chong, Chen's Shen Wena, Zhou Hongzheng, and Zhang Ji, Sui's He Tuo and Liu Xuan, and others — to be reported; they would receive promotion and elevation.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yi-wei an edict called for descendants of eminent scholars of recent dynasties — including Huangfu Kan and Chu Zhongdu of Liang, Xiong Ansheng and Shen Chong of Zhou, Shen Wena, Zhou Hongzheng, and Zhang Ji of Chen, and He Tuo and Liu Xuan of Sui — to be identified and given preferment.

sentences.zh: 三月，竇州道行軍總管黨仁弘擊羅竇反獠，破之，俘七千餘口。

translations.literal: In the third month, Campaign Commander of the Daozhou Circuit Dang Renhong attacked the rebel Liao of Luozhou, defeated them, and captured more than seven thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Campaign Commander Dang Renhong of the Daozhou Circuit attacked the rebel Liao tribes of Luozhou, routed them, and took more than seven thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，流鬼國遣使入貢。

translations.literal: On the day xin-chou, the state of Liugui sent envoys to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xin-chou envoys from Liugui arrived to pay tribute.

sentences.zh: 去京師萬五千里，濱於北海，南鄰靺鞨，未嘗通中國，重三譯而來。

translations.literal: It was fifteen thousand li from the capital, bordered the Northern Sea, adjoined Mohe to the south, had never communicated with China, and came via triple translation.
translations.idiomatic: Liugui lay fifteen thousand li from the capital, on the shores of the Northern Sea and bordering Mohe to the south. It had never before been in contact with the empire; the envoys required three successive interpreters.

sentences.zh: 上以其使者佘志為騎都尉。

translations.literal: The emperor made its envoy She Zhi Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed its envoy She Zhi Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，置寧朔大使以護突厥。

translations.literal: On the day bing-chen, a Pacification of the North Commissioner was established to protect the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bing-chen the post of Pacification Commissioner of the North was created to oversee the Turks.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，壬寅，徙燕王靈夔為魯王。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on the day ren-yin, Prince of Yan Lingkai was transferred to be Prince of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on the day ren-yin, Prince of Yan Li Lingkai was reassigned as Prince of Lu.

sentences.zh: 上將幸洛陽，命將作大匠閻立德行清暑之地。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to visit Luoyang and ordered Master of Works Yan Lide to seek a place to escape the summer heat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor planned a visit to Luoyang and ordered Master of Works Yan Lide to locate a site for a summer retreat.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，庚午，作襄城宮於汝州西山。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on the day geng-wu, Xiangcheng Palace was built on the western hills of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on the day geng-wu, construction began on Xiangcheng Palace in the western hills of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 立德，立本之兄也。

translations.literal: Lide was Liben's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Lide was the elder brother of the painter Yan Liben.

sentences.zh: 高昌王文泰聞唐兵起，謂其國人曰：「唐去我七千里，沙磧居其二千里，地無水草，寒風如刀，熱風如燒，安能致大軍乎！

translations.literal: Gaochang King Wenkai, hearing that Tang troops were mobilized, said to his people: "Tang is seven thousand li from us; desert occupies two thousand li of that. The land has no water or grass — cold winds cut like knives, hot winds burn like fire. How can they bring a great army!
translations.idiomatic: When King Wenkai of Gaochang learned that Tang forces were marching, he told his people: "Tang is seven thousand li away, and two thousand of those are desert without water or grass. Cold winds cut like knives; hot winds scorch like fire. How could they possibly move a large army against us?

sentences.zh: 往吾入朝，見秦、隴之北，城邑蕭條，非復有隋之比。

translations.literal: When I previously entered court, I saw north of Qin and Long — cities and towns desolate and empty, no longer comparable to Sui times.
translations.idiomatic: When I last visited the court, the towns north of Qin and Long were hollow and desolate — nothing like they had been under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 今來伐我，發兵多則糧運不給；

translations.literal: Now coming to attack us — if they send out many troops, grain transport will not suffice;
translations.idiomatic: If they send a large force, they cannot supply it;

sentences.zh: 三萬已下，吾力能制之。

translations.literal: Thirty thousand or fewer — my strength can control them.
translations.idiomatic: anything under thirty thousand men, we can handle.

sentences.zh: 當以逸待勞，坐收其弊。

translations.literal: One should await them at ease while they are weary, and sit to harvest their exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: We need only wait at ease while they exhaust themselves.

sentences.zh: 若頓兵城下，不過二十日，食盡必走，然後從而虜之。

translations.literal: If they halt troops below the walls, within no more than twenty days food will be exhausted and they must flee — then follow and capture them.
translations.idiomatic: If they camp beneath our walls, within twenty days their supplies will run out and they will retreat — then we can follow and seize them.

sentences.zh: 何足憂也！」

translations.literal: What is there worth worrying about!"
translations.idiomatic: What is there to fear?"

sentences.zh: 及聞唐兵臨磧口，憂懼不知所為，發疾卒，子智盛立。

translations.literal: When he heard that Tang troops had reached the desert pass, he was anxious and fearful and knew not what to do. Illness erupted and he died. His son Zhicheng succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: But when he learned that Tang troops had reached the desert pass, fear overwhelmed him. He fell ill and died, and his son Qu Zhicheng succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 軍至柳谷，詗者言文泰刻日將葬，國人咸集於彼，諸將請襲之，侯君集曰：「不可，天子以高昌無禮，故使吾討之，今襲人於墟墓之間，非問罪之師也。」

translations.literal: When the army reached Willow Valley, scouts reported that Wenkai had fixed a day for burial and the people of the state all gathered there. The generals requested a surprise attack. Hou Junji said: "It cannot be done. The Son of Heaven sent us because Gaochang was disrespectful, yet to attack men amid tombs and burial grounds is not an army that comes to demand account of crimes."
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Willow Valley, scouts reported that Wenkai's funeral was set for a fixed day and the whole kingdom would gather there. The generals urged a surprise attack. Hou Junji refused: "The Son of Heaven sent us because Gaochang showed contempt for the court. Striking mourners among the tombs is not how a punitive expedition conducts itself."

sentences.zh: 於是鼓行而進，至田城，諭之，不下，詰朝攻之，及午而克，虜男女七千餘口。

translations.literal: Thereupon they beat drums and advanced. Reaching Tiancheng, they instructed surrender — it did not submit. At dawn the next day they attacked; by noon it was taken, and more than seven thousand men and women were captured.
translations.idiomatic: The army marched forward to Tiancheng and called for surrender. The city refused. At dawn the next day they attacked; by noon it had fallen, and more than seven thousand people were taken.

sentences.zh: 以中郎將辛獠兒為前鋒，夜，趨其都城，高昌逆戰而敗，大軍繼至，抵其城下。

translations.literal: Middle General Xin Laor was made vanguard. By night they rushed to the capital. Gaochang met them in battle and was defeated. The main army followed and reached below the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: Middle General Xin Laor led the vanguard. By night they pressed on to the capital. Gaochang met them in battle and was routed. The main force arrived and encamped beneath the walls.

sentences.zh: 智盛致書於君集曰：「得罪於天子者，先王也，天罰所加，身已物故。

translations.literal: Zhicheng sent a letter to Junji saying: "The one who offended the Son of Heaven was the former king. Heaven's punishment fell upon him; his person is already deceased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicheng wrote to Hou Junji: "It was my father who offended the Son of Heaven. Heaven's judgment has fallen — he is already dead.

sentences.zh: 智盛襲位未幾，惟尚書憐察。」

translations.literal: Zhicheng has succeeded to the throne only recently — I only beg the minister's compassionate consideration."
translations.idiomatic: I have only just succeeded him. I beg your mercy."

sentences.zh: 君集報曰：「苟能悔過，當束手軍門。」

translations.literal: Junji replied: "If you can repent, you should bind your hands at the army gate."
translations.idiomatic: Hou Junji replied: "If you truly repent, come out and surrender at the gate."

sentences.zh: 智盛猶不出。

translations.literal: Zhicheng still did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicheng still refused to surrender.

sentences.zh: 君集命填塹攻之，飛石雨下，城中人皆室處。

translations.literal: Junji ordered the moat filled and an assault launched. Flying stones rained down; the people in the city all remained indoors.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Junji ordered the moats filled and the assault begun. Stones rained from catapults; the townspeople hid indoors.

sentences.zh: 又為巢車，高十丈，俯瞰城中。

translations.literal: Siege towers were also built, ten zhang high, overlooking the city.
translations.idiomatic: Siege towers ten zhang high were built to overlook the city.

sentences.zh: 有行人及飛石所中，皆唱言之。

translations.literal: Whenever passersby were struck by flying stones, all proclaimed it aloud.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever anyone in the streets was struck by a falling stone, the attackers shouted the news from the towers.

sentences.zh: 先是，文泰與西突厥可汗相結，約有急相助；

translations.literal: Earlier, Wenkai had allied with the Western Türk qaghan, agreeing that in emergency they would aid each other;
translations.idiomatic: Wenkai had earlier allied with the Western Türk qaghan, pledging mutual aid in time of need;

sentences.zh: 可汗遣其葉護屯可汗浮圖城，為文泰聲援。

translations.literal: The qaghan sent his yabgu to garrison at Qaghan Fotucheng as reinforcement for Wenkai.
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan had sent his yabgu to hold Qaghan Fotucheng in support of Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 及君集至，可汗懼而西走千餘里，葉護以城降。

translations.literal: When Junji arrived, the qaghan feared and fled west more than a thousand li; the yabgu surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Junji arrived, the qaghan fled westward more than a thousand li in fear, and the yabgu surrendered the fortress.

sentences.zh: 智盛窮蹙，癸酉，開門出降。

translations.literal: Zhicheng, hard pressed, on the day gui-you opened the gates and came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Driven to desperation, on the day gui-you Zhicheng opened the gates and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 君集分兵略地，下其二十二城，戶八千四十六，口一萬七千七百，地東西八百里，南北五百里。

translations.literal: Junji divided his troops to seize territory, taking twenty-two of their cities, with eight thousand forty-six households, seventeen thousand seven hundred persons, and land eight hundred li east to west and five hundred li north to south.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Junji sent detachments to overrun the countryside, capturing twenty-two cities—eight thousand forty-six households and seventeen thousand seven hundred people—over a stretch eight hundred li from east to west and five hundred li from north to south.

sentences.zh: 上欲以高昌為州縣，魏徵諫曰：「陛下初即位，文泰夫婦首來朝，其後稍驕倨，故王誅加之。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to make Gaochang into prefectures and counties. Wei Zheng remonstrated, saying: "When Your Majesty first ascended the throne, Wen Tai and his wife were the first to come to court. Afterwards they grew somewhat arrogant and insolent, and therefore the king's punishment was applied to them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor planned to annex Gaochang as prefectures and counties. Wei Zheng objected: "When Your Majesty first took the throne, Qu Wentai and his wife were the first to pay homage at court. Later they grew arrogant, and so royal punishment fell upon them.

sentences.zh: 罪止文泰可矣，宜撫其百姓，存其社稷，復立其子，則威德被於遐荒，四夷皆悅服矣。

translations.literal: The crime should stop with Wen Tai alone. Your Majesty ought to comfort their common people, preserve their altars of soil and grain, and restore their son to the throne. Then authority and virtue would reach the far wilderness, and the four barbarians would all gladly submit.
translations.idiomatic: Wentai alone deserved punishment. Your Majesty should reassure the people, preserve their state, and restore his son to the throne. Then your majesty and mercy would reach the remotest lands, and all the frontier peoples would gladly submit.

sentences.zh: 今若利其土地以為州縣，則常須千餘人鎮守，數年一易，往來死者什有三四，供辦衣資，違離親戚，十年之後，隴右虛耗矣。

translations.literal: If now you take their land for profit and make it prefectures and counties, then more than a thousand men will constantly be needed to garrison it, rotated every few years. Of those coming and going, three or four in ten die on the road. Provisioning clothing and supplies, separated from kin—after ten years, Longyou will be drained empty.
translations.idiomatic: If you seize their land and turn it into prefectures and counties, you will need more than a thousand men to garrison it at all times, rotated every few years. Three or four in ten of those sent back and forth will die on the road. They must be clothed and supplied, torn from their families—and within ten years Longyou will be exhausted.

sentences.zh: 陛下終不得高昌撮粟尺帛以佐中國，所謂散有用以事無用。

translations.literal: Your Majesty would in the end never obtain from Gaochang even a pinch of grain or a foot of cloth to assist the Central Kingdom. This is what is called dispersing what is useful to serve what is useless.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty would never see so much as a pinch of grain or a foot of cloth from Gaochang to aid the heartland. You would be scattering what is useful to sustain what is useless.

sentences.zh: 臣未見其可。」

translations.literal: Your servant does not see how this can be approved."
translations.idiomatic: I see no merit in it."

sentences.zh: 上不從，九月，以其地為西州，以可汗浮圖城為庭州，各置屬縣，乙卯，置安西都護府於交河城，留兵鎮之。

translations.literal: The emperor did not follow this advice. In the ninth month he made the territory into Xizhou Prefecture and Keshan Fotucheng into Tingzhou Prefecture, establishing subordinate counties in each. On the day yimao he established the Protectorate General of Anxi at Jiaohe City and left troops to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not be persuaded. In the ninth month he made the territory Xizhou Prefecture and Keshan Fotucheng Tingzhou Prefecture, each with its own subordinate counties. On the day yimao he established the Protectorate General of Anxi at Jiaohe and left troops to hold it.

sentences.zh: 君集虜高昌王智盛及其群臣豪傑而還。

translations.literal: Junji took captive the King of Gaochang, Zhisheng, along with his ministers and leading men, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Junji marched home with Gaochang's king Zhisheng and his ministers and notables as captives.

sentences.zh: 於是唐地東極於海，西至焉耆，南盡林邑，北抵大漠，皆為州縣，凡東西九千五百一十里，南北一萬九百一十八里。

translations.literal: Thereupon Tang territory reached east to the sea, west to Yanqi, south to Linyi, and north to the great desert—all made into prefectures and counties. In all it was nine thousand five hundred ten li east to west and ten thousand ninety-eight li north to south.
translations.idiomatic: Tang territory now ran east to the sea, west to Yanqi, south to Linyi, and north to the great desert—all organized as prefectures and counties. From east to west it measured nine thousand five hundred ten li; from north to south, ten thousand ninety-eight li.

sentences.zh: 侯君集之討高昌也，遣使約焉耆與之合勢，焉耆喜，聽命。

translations.literal: When Hou Junji was campaigning against Gaochang, he sent envoys to arrange with Yanqi to join forces. Yanqi was pleased and obeyed his command.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Junji marched against Gaochang, he sent envoys to Yanqi proposing a joint attack. Yanqi gladly agreed.

sentences.zh: 及高昌破，焉耆王詣軍門謁見君集，且言焉耆三城先為高昌所奪，君集奏並高昌所掠焉耆民悉歸之。

translations.literal: When Gaochang fell, the King of Yanqi came to the army gate to pay respects to Junji and stated that three Yanqi cities had earlier been seized by Gaochang. Junji memorialized that all Yanqi people taken by Gaochang should be returned.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaochang fell, the king of Yanqi came to the camp to pay his respects to Hou Junji and reported that Gaochang had seized three Yanqi cities. Junji memorialized that all Yanqi people carried off by Gaochang should be restored.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲戌，荊王元景等復表請封禪，上不許。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day jiaxu, Prince Jing Yuanjing and others again submitted a memorial requesting the feng and shan rites. The emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the day jiaxu, Prince Jing of Jing, Yuan Jing, and others again petitioned for the feng and shan rites at Mount Tai. The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 初，陳倉折衝都尉魯寧坐事繫獄，自恃高班，慢罵陳倉尉尉氏劉仁軌，仁軌杖殺之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Lu Ning, Colonel of the Resolute Assault at Chencang, was imprisoned for an offense. Trusting in his high rank, he insulted and reviled Liu Renji of Weishi, the assistant magistrate of Chencang. Renji beat him to death with a staff.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Lu Ning, Colonel of the Resolute Assault at Chencang, had been jailed for an offense. Counting on his high rank, he insulted Liu Renji, assistant magistrate of Chencang County in Weishi. Renji beat him to death with a staff.

sentences.zh: 州司以聞。

translations.literal: The prefectural office reported this to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural authorities reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 上怒，命斬之，怒猶不解，曰：「何物縣尉，敢殺吾折衝！」

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and ordered Renji executed. His anger still unappeased, he said: "What sort of county assistant is this, that he dares kill my Colonel of the Resolute Assault!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered Renji executed. Still not satisfied, he said: "What kind of county assistant dares kill my Colonel of the Resolute Assault!"

sentences.zh: 命追至長安面詰之。

translations.literal: He ordered Renji pursued to Chang'an to be questioned face to face.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Renji brought to Chang'an to answer for himself in person.

sentences.zh: 仁軌曰：「魯寧對臣百姓辱臣如此，臣實忿而殺之。」

translations.literal: Renji said: "Lu Ning, in the presence of the common people, insulted me in this way. Your servant was truly enraged and killed him."
translations.idiomatic: Renji said: "Lu Ning humiliated me like this before the people. I was so enraged that I killed him."

sentences.zh: 辭色自若。

translations.literal: His words and bearing were entirely composed.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke without the least sign of fear.

sentences.zh: 魏徵侍側，曰：「陛下知隋之所以亡乎？」

translations.literal: Wei Zheng, attending at his side, said: "Does Your Majesty know why Sui perished?"
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng, standing at the emperor's side, said: "Does Your Majesty know why the Sui fell?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「何也？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Why?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked: "Why?"

sentences.zh: 征曰：「隋末，百姓強而陵官吏，如魯寧之比是也。」

translations.literal: Zheng said: "At the end of Sui, the common people were strong and overbearing toward officials—men like Lu Ning were the reason."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng said: "At the end of the Sui, commoners were strong enough to bully officials—men like Lu Ning were the reason."

sentences.zh: 上悅，擢仁軌為櫟陽丞。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and promoted Renji to Assistant Magistrate of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and promoted Renji to assistant magistrate of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 上將幸同州校獵，仁軌上言：「今秋大稔，民收穫者才一二，使之供承獵事，治道葺橋，動費一二萬功，實妨農事。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to visit Tongzhou for a hunting expedition. Renji submitted a memorial saying: "This autumn the harvest is abundant, yet the people have gathered only one or two parts in ten. If they are made to supply the hunting expedition and repair roads and bridges, the labor easily costs ten or twenty thousand man-days. It truly obstructs agricultural work.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to go to Tongzhou for a hunting expedition. Renji memorialized: "This autumn's harvest is abundant, yet the people have gathered only a tenth or two of the crop. If they must serve the hunt and repair roads and bridges, the work will cost ten or twenty thousand man-days and seriously interfere with farming.

sentences.zh: 願少停鑾輿旬日，俟其畢務，則公私俱濟。」

translations.literal: I beg that the imperial carriage pause for ten days or so, waiting until their work is finished. Then both public and private affairs will benefit together."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to delay the journey ten days or so, until the harvest is in. Then both state and people will be served."

sentences.zh: 上賜璽書嘉納之，尋遷新安令。

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed an imperial edict commending and accepting his advice, and soon transferred him to Magistrate of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an edict praising and accepting his advice, and soon appointed him magistrate of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 閏月，乙未，行幸同州；

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on the day yimao, he traveled to Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on the day yimao, the emperor traveled to Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，還宮。

translations.literal: On the day gengxu he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengxu he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，吐蕃贊普遣其相祿東贊獻金五千兩及珍玩數百，以請婚。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, the Tibetan tsenpo sent his minister Gar Tongtsen, presenting five thousand taels of gold and several hundred precious curios, to request a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingchen, the Tibetan ruler sent his minister Gar Tongtsen with five thousand taels of gold and several hundred precious objects to request a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 上許以文成公主妻之。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed to give Princess Wencheng in marriage to him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed to give Princess Wencheng to him in marriage.

sentences.zh: 十一月，甲子朔，冬至，上祀南郊。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the first day jiazi, the winter solstice, the emperor sacrificed at the Southern Altar.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the first day jiazi—the winter solstice—the emperor sacrificed at the Southern Altar.

sentences.zh: 時《戊寅歷》以癸亥為朔，宣義郎李淳風表稱：「古歷分日起於子半，今歲甲子朔冬至，而故太史令傅仁均減餘稍多，子初為朔，遂差三刻，用乖天正，請更加考定。」

translations.literal: At that time the Wuyin Calendar took guihai as the new moon. Gentleman for Promoting Righteousness Li Chunfeng submitted a memorial stating: "The ancient calendar reckoned the day from the middle of the zi hour. This year, on the jiazi new moon at the winter solstice, the late Director of the Astronomy Bureau Fu Renjun reduced the remainder somewhat too much, making the start of the zi hour the new moon. The result was a discrepancy of three quarters of an hour, departing from the true celestial standard. I request further examination and correction."
translations.idiomatic: The Wuyin Calendar then placed the new moon on guihai. Gentleman for Promoting Righteousness Li Chunfeng memorialized: "Ancient calendars reckoned the day from the middle of the zi hour. This year the jiazi new moon fell on the winter solstice, but the late Director of the Astronomy Bureau Fu Renjun had trimmed the remainder too far, making the new moon fall at the start of the zi hour—a discrepancy of three quarters of an hour from the true celestial reckoning. I ask that this be examined and corrected."

sentences.zh: 眾議以仁均定朔微差，淳風推校精密，請如淳風議，從之。

translations.literal: The assembled discussion held that Renjun's fixing of the new moon was slightly off, while Chunfeng's calculations were precise. They requested that Chunfeng's proposal be followed, and the emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The assembled officials judged Renjun's new-moon calculation slightly off and Chunfeng's recalculation precise. They asked that Chunfeng's proposal be adopted, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，禮官奏請加高祖父母服齊衰五月，嫡子婦服期，嫂、叔、弟妻、夫兄、舅皆服小功；

translations.literal: On the day dingmao, the ritual officials memorialized requesting that mourning for the emperor's paternal grandparents be increased to qi mourning for five months; that a principal son's wife wear one-year mourning; and that elder brother's wife, younger brother's wife, husband's elder brother, and maternal uncle all wear xiao gong mourning.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingmao, the ritual officials memorialized that mourning for the emperor's paternal grandparents be set at qi mourning for five months; that a principal son's wife wear one-year mourning; and that elder brother's wife, younger brother's wife, husband's elder brother, and maternal uncle all wear xiao gong mourning.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 丙子，百官復表請封禪，詔許之。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi, the hundred officials again submitted memorials requesting the feng and shan rites. An edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingzi, the officials again petitioned for the feng and shan rites. An edict granted their request.

sentences.zh: 更命諸儒詳定儀注；

translations.literal: The emperor further ordered the various scholars to determine the ritual regulations in detail.
translations.idiomatic: He further ordered the scholars to work out the ritual regulations in detail.

sentences.zh: 以太常卿韋挺等為封禪使。

translations.literal: He appointed the Minister of Rites Wei Ting and others as commissioners for the feng and shan rites.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Minister of Rites Wei Ting and others commissioners for the feng and shan rites.

sentences.zh: 司門員外郎韋元方給給使過所稽緩，給使奏之；

translations.literal: Wei Yuanfang, Vice Director in the Department of the Gate, was slow in issuing travel permits to imperial messengers. The messengers reported this.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuanfang, Vice Director in the Department of the Gate, was slow in issuing travel permits to imperial messengers, and they reported him.

sentences.zh: 上怒，出元方為華陰令。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and demoted Yuanfang to Magistrate of Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and demoted Yuanfang to magistrate of Huayin.

sentences.zh: 魏徵諫曰：「帝王震怒，不可妄發。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng remonstrated, saying: "When an emperor's wrath is aroused, it must not be released rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng objected: "An emperor's anger must not be vented lightly.

sentences.zh: 前為給使，遂夜出敕書，事如軍機，誰不驚駭！

translations.literal: Earlier, for the sake of a messenger, an edict was issued in the middle of the night, handled like urgent military business. Who would not be alarmed!
translations.idiomatic: For a messenger's complaint, an edict went out in the middle of the night as if it were urgent military business. Who would not be terrified!

sentences.zh: 況宦者之徒，古來難養，輕為言語，易生患害，獨行遠使，深非事宜，漸不可長，所宜深慎。」

translations.literal: Moreover, eunuchs and their kind have from ancient times been hard to keep in hand. They speak lightly and easily give rise to harm. Sending them alone on distant missions is deeply unsuitable. This practice must not be allowed to grow. Your Majesty ought to be deeply cautious."
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs have always been hard to control. They speak lightly and easily stir up trouble. Sending them alone on distant missions is deeply unwise. The practice must not be allowed to grow. Your Majesty should be very careful."

sentences.zh: 上納其言。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his advice.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞韋悰句司農木橦價貴於民間，奏其隱沒。

translations.literal: Wei Cong, Left Assistant Director in the Department of State Affairs, investigated the Ministry of Revenue's cotton price and found it higher than the market price. He memorialized that the ministry was concealing wrongdoing.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Cong, Left Assistant Director in the Department of State Affairs, investigated the Ministry of Revenue's cotton price and found it higher than the market rate. He memorialized that the ministry was concealing wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 上召大理卿孫伏伽書司農罪。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned the Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review, Sun Fuga, to write out the Ministry of Revenue's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review Sun Fuga to draft charges against the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 伏伽曰：「司農無罪。」

translations.literal: Fuga said: "The Ministry of Revenue is not guilty."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fuga said: "The Ministry of Revenue is not guilty."

sentences.zh: 上怪，問其故，對曰：「只為官橦貴，所以私橦賤。

translations.literal: The emperor was puzzled and asked the reason. He replied: "It is only because official cotton is expensive that private cotton is cheap.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was astonished and asked why. He replied: "Official cotton is priced high, so private cotton is cheap.

sentences.zh: 向使官橦賤，私橦無由賤矣。

translations.literal: If official cotton were cheap, private cotton would have no way to be cheap.
translations.idiomatic: If official cotton were priced low, private cotton could not be sold cheaply.

sentences.zh: 但見司農識大體，不知其過也。」

translations.literal: One only sees that the Ministry of Revenue understood the larger principle and did not know its fault."
translations.idiomatic: The ministry understood the larger principle. That is no fault."

sentences.zh: 上悟，屢稱其善；

translations.literal: The emperor understood and repeatedly praised his insight.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw the point and praised him repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 顧謂韋悰曰：「卿識用不逮伏伽遠矣。」

translations.literal: Turning, he said to Wei Cong: "Your insight and ability fall far short of Fuga's."
translations.idiomatic: Turning to Wei Cong, he said: "Your judgment is far inferior to Sun Fuga's."

sentences.zh: 十二月，丁酉，侯君集獻俘於觀德殿。
