translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day dingyou, Hou Junji presented captives at the Hall for Observing Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day dingyou, Hou Junji presented his captives at the Hall for Observing Virtue.

sentences.zh: 行飲至禮，大酺三日。

translations.literal: The ceremony of drinking on arrival was performed, and a great feast was held for three days.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremony of drinking on arrival was performed, and the court feasted for three days.

sentences.zh: 尋以智盛為左武衛將軍、金城郡公。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Zhisheng was made General of the Left Martial Guard and Duke of Jincheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Zhisheng was made General of the Left Martial Guard and Duke of Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 上得高昌樂工，以付太常，增九部樂為十部。

translations.literal: The emperor obtained Gaochang musicians and entrusted them to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, increasing the Nine Departments of Music to ten.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took Gaochang's musicians into the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and expanded the Nine Departments of Music to ten.

sentences.zh: 君集之破高昌也，私取其珍寶；

translations.literal: When Junji destroyed Gaochang, he privately took its precious treasures.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Junji conquered Gaochang, he privately seized its treasures.

sentences.zh: 將士知之，競為盜竊，君集不能禁，為有司所劾，詔下君集等獄。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers knew of this and competed in plunder. Junji could not restrain them. He was impeached by the responsible officials, and an edict sent Junji and others to prison.
translations.idiomatic: The troops knew of it and plundered freely. Junji could not stop them. The responsible officials impeached him, and an edict sent Junji and his men to prison.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎岑文本上疏，以為：「高昌昏迷，陛下命君集等討而克之，不逾旬日，並付大理。

translations.literal: Cen Wenben, Vice Director of the Secretariat, submitted a memorial stating: "Gaochang was benighted and deluded. Your Majesty ordered Junji and others to campaign against it and conquer it in less than ten days. Yet now all have been handed over to the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Wenben, Vice Director of the Secretariat, memorialized: "Gaochang was benighted. Your Majesty sent Hou Junji and his men to conquer it in less than ten days. Yet now they have all been handed over to the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 雖君集等自掛網羅，恐海內之人疑陛下唯錄其過，而遺其功也。

translations.literal: Although Junji and the others brought the net upon themselves, I fear people throughout the realm will suspect that Your Majesty records only their faults and forgets their achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Though Junji and the others brought this on themselves, I fear people throughout the realm will suspect that Your Majesty records only their faults and forgets their achievements.

sentences.zh: 臣聞命將出師，主於克敵，苟能克敵，雖貪可賞；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that when generals are ordered to take the field, the main point is to defeat the enemy. If they can defeat the enemy, even if greedy they may be rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when generals are sent to war, the point is to defeat the enemy. If they defeat the enemy, even the greedy may be rewarded.

sentences.zh: 若其敗績，雖廉可誅。

translations.literal: If they suffer defeat, even if incorrupt they may be punished.
translations.idiomatic: If they are defeated, even the incorrupt may be punished.

sentences.zh: 是以漢之李廣利、陳湯，晉之王浚，隋之韓擒虎，皆負罪譴，人主以其有功，鹹受封賞。

translations.literal: Therefore in Han, Li Guangli and Chen Tang; in Jin, Wang Jun; in Sui, Han Qihu—all bore guilt and censure, yet their rulers, because they had achievements, all received enfeoffment and reward.
translations.idiomatic: That is why in Han, Li Guangli and Chen Tang; in Jin, Wang Jun; in Sui, Han Qihu—all were guilty and censured, yet their rulers rewarded them for their achievements.

sentences.zh: 由是觀之，將帥之臣，廉慎者寡，貪求者眾。

translations.literal: Viewed from this, among generals and commanders, those who are incorrupt and cautious are few; those who are greedy and grasping are many.
translations.idiomatic: Seen in this light, among commanders the incorrupt and cautious are few, the greedy and grasping many.

sentences.zh: 是以黃石公《軍勢》曰：『使智，使勇，使貪，使愚，故智者樂立其功，勇者好行其志，貪者急趨其利，愚者不計其死。』

translations.literal: Therefore Master Yellow Rock's Military Dispositions says: 'Employ the wise, employ the brave, employ the greedy, employ the foolish. Thus the wise delight in establishing their achievements, the brave love to carry out their will, the greedy hurry after profit, and the foolish do not count the cost of death.'
translations.idiomatic: Master Yellow Rock's Military Dispositions says: 'Employ the wise, the brave, the greedy, and the foolish. The wise delight in winning glory; the brave love to follow their will; the greedy hurry after profit; the foolish do not count the cost of death.'

sentences.zh: 伏願錄其微勞，忘其大過，使君集重升朝列，復備驅馳，雖非清貞之臣，猶得貪愚之將，斯則陛下雖屈法而德彌顯，君集等雖蒙宥而過更彰矣。」

translations.literal: I humbly wish that Your Majesty record their slight merit and forget their great fault, restoring Junji to the court ranks and again employing him on campaign. Though he is not a pure and upright minister, he may still serve as a greedy and foolish general. Then Your Majesty, though bending the law, would show virtue all the more clearly, and Junji and the others, though pardoned, would have their faults made all the more plain."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to record their slight merit and overlook their great fault, restore Junji to court rank, and employ him again on campaign. Though not a pure and upright minister, he may still serve as a greedy and foolish general. Then Your Majesty, though bending the law, would show virtue all the more clearly, and Junji and the others, though pardoned, would have their faults made all the plainer."

sentences.zh: 上乃釋之。

translations.literal: The emperor then released them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then released them.

sentences.zh: 又有告薛萬均私通高昌婦女者，萬均不服，內出高昌婦女付大理，與萬均對辯，魏徵諫曰：「臣聞『君使臣以禮，臣事君以忠。』

translations.literal: There was also a report that Xue Wanjun had privately consorted with a Gaochang woman. Wanjun would not admit it. The palace sent out the Gaochang woman to the Court of Judicial Review to confront and debate with Wanjun. Wei Zheng remonstrated, saying: "Your servant has heard, 'The ruler employs his ministers with propriety; ministers serve their ruler with loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Someone also reported that Xue Wanjun had had an affair with a Gaochang woman. Wanjun denied it. The palace sent the woman to the Court of Judicial Review to confront him. Wei Zheng objected: "I have heard that 'the ruler employs his ministers with propriety; ministers serve their ruler with loyalty.

sentences.zh: 今遣大將軍與亡國婦女對辯帷箔之私，實則所得者輕，虛則所失者重。

translations.literal: Now to send a great general to confront and debate with a woman of a destroyed state over private matters behind curtains and screens—even if what is gained is real, it is slight; even if the offense is unsubstantiated, what is lost is grave.
translations.idiomatic: To send a great general to argue with a woman of a conquered state over private matters behind the curtain—even if something real is gained, it is slight; the intangible loss is grave.

sentences.zh: 昔秦穆飲盜馬之士，楚莊赦絕纓之罪，況陛下道高堯、舜，而曾二君之不逮乎！」

translations.literal: Formerly Duke Mu of Qin feasted the man who stole his horse, and King Zhuang of Chu pardoned the offense of the man who snapped his tassel. How much more should Your Majesty, whose Way surpasses Yao and Shun, fail to match those two rulers!"
translations.idiomatic: Duke Mu of Qin once rewarded the man who stole his horse; King Zhuang of Chu pardoned the man who snapped his tassel. Your Majesty's virtue surpasses Yao and Shun—surely you need not fall short of those two rulers!"

sentences.zh: 上遽釋之。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately released Wanjun.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately released him.

sentences.zh: 侯君集馬病□顙，行軍總管趙元楷親以指沾其膿而嗅之，御史劾奏其諂，左遷括州刺史。

translations.literal: Hou Junji's horse had a maggot-infested sore on its forehead. Zhao Yuankai, Commander of the Campaign, personally dipped his finger in the pus and smelled it. The censor impeached him for fawning and demoted him to Prefect of Kuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Junji's horse had a maggot-infested sore on its forehead. Zhao Yuankai, Commander of the Campaign, dipped his finger in the pus and smelled it. The censor impeached him for fawning and demoted him to prefect of Kuozhou.

sentences.zh: 高昌之平也，諸將皆即受賞，行軍總管阿史那社爾以無敕旨，獨不受，及別敕既下，乃受之，所取唯老弱故弊而已。

translations.literal: When Gaochang was pacified, all the generals immediately accepted rewards. Ashina She'er, Commander of the Campaign, because there was no imperial edict, alone refused to accept. Only after a separate edict was issued did he accept, taking only what was old, weak, worn, and broken.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaochang was pacified, the generals all accepted rewards at once. Ashina She'er, Commander of the Campaign, refused because no imperial edict had yet been issued. Only after a separate edict arrived did he accept—and then took only what was old, weak, and worn out.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其廉慎，以高昌所得寶刀及雜彩千段賜之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his incorruptibility and caution, and bestowed on him a precious sword taken from Gaochang and a thousand bolts of assorted silks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his integrity and gave him a precious sword taken from Gaochang and a thousand bolts of assorted silks.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，上獵於樊川；

translations.literal: On the day guimao the emperor hunted at Fanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guimao the emperor hunted at Fanchuan.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，還宮。

translations.literal: On the day yisi he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yisi he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 魏徵上疏，以為：「在朝群臣，當樞機之寄者，任之雖重，信之未篤，是以人或自疑，心懷苟且。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng submitted a memorial stating: "Among the ministers at court who bear the charge of the pivot of state, though their responsibilities are weighty, trust in them is not yet deep. Therefore some harbor self-doubt and keep their hearts in a state of compromise.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng memorialized: "Among the ministers who bear the weight of state affairs, responsibilities are heavy but trust is not yet deep. Some doubt themselves and keep their hearts in compromise.

sentences.zh: 陛下寬於大事，急於小罪，臨時責怒，未免愛憎。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is lenient on great matters and urgent over small offenses, assigning blame and anger on the spot, not free from favor and dislike.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is lenient over great matters and harsh over small offenses, rebuking officials on the spot without escaping favor and dislike.

sentences.zh: 夫委大臣以大體，責小臣以小事，為治之道也。

translations.literal: To entrust great ministers with the larger principles and charge lesser officials with small matters—this is the way of good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Entrust great ministers with the larger principles and charge lesser officials with small matters—that is the way to govern.

sentences.zh: 今委之以職，則重大臣而輕小臣；

translations.literal: Now when you entrust them with office, you value great ministers and slight lesser ones.
translations.idiomatic: In appointing them to office, you honor great ministers and slight lesser ones.

sentences.zh: 至於有事，則信小臣而疑大臣。

translations.literal: But when something arises, you trust lesser officials and doubt great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: But when trouble arises, you trust lesser officials and doubt great ministers.

sentences.zh: 信其所輕，疑其所重，將求致治，其可得乎！

translations.literal: Trusting those you slight and doubting those you value—if you seek to bring about good order, how can it be attained!
translations.idiomatic: Trusting those you slight and doubting those you honor—how can good order come of that!

sentences.zh: 若任以大官，求其細過，刀筆之吏，順旨承風，舞文弄法，曲成其罪。

translations.literal: If you appoint them to high office and then seek out their minute faults, the clerks with their pens, following your intent and catching the wind of your mood, manipulate the law and twist texts to contrive their guilt.
translations.idiomatic: If you give them high office and then hunt for minute faults, the clerks will follow your mood, twist the law, and contrive their guilt.

sentences.zh: 自陳也，則以為心不伏辜；

translations.literal: If they confess themselves, it is taken as their hearts not accepting guilt.
translations.idiomatic: If they confess, it is taken as unwillingness to accept guilt.

sentences.zh: 不言也，則以為所犯皆實；

translations.literal: If they do not speak, it is taken that all the offenses charged are real.
translations.idiomatic: If they stay silent, it is taken that every charge is true.

sentences.zh: 進退惟谷，莫能自明，則苟求免禍，矯偽成俗矣。」

translations.literal: Advancing or retreating, they are trapped in peril and cannot clarify themselves. Then they seek only to escape disaster, and pretense becomes custom."
translations.idiomatic: Whether they advance or retreat, they are trapped and cannot clear themselves. Then they seek only to escape harm, and pretense becomes the custom."

sentences.zh: 上納之。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 上謂侍臣曰：「朕雖平定天下，其守之甚難。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to his attending officials: "Although I have pacified the realm, keeping it is very difficult."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his attendants: "Although I have pacified the realm, keeping it is very hard."

sentences.zh: 魏徵對曰：「臣聞戰勝易，守勝難，陛下之及此言，宗廟社稷之福也！」

translations.literal: Wei Zheng replied: "Your servant has heard that winning in battle is easy, but winning in keeping is hard. That Your Majesty has reached this saying is a blessing for the ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain!"
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng replied: "I have heard that winning in battle is easy but winning in peace is hard. That Your Majesty can say this is a blessing for the ancestral temple and the state!"

sentences.zh: 上聞右庶子張玄素在東宮數諫爭，擢為銀青光祿大夫，行左庶子。

translations.literal: The emperor heard that Zhang Xuansu, Right Guardian of the Heir Apparent, had repeatedly remonstrated and argued in the Eastern Palace. He promoted him to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the Silver Seal and made him Acting Left Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Zhang Xuansu, Right Guardian of the Heir Apparent, had repeatedly remonstrated in the Eastern Palace, the emperor promoted him to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the Silver Seal and made him Acting Left Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 太子嘗於宮中擊鼓，玄素叩閣切諫；

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent once beat drums in the palace. Xuansu knocked at the gate and remonstrated sharply.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince once beat drums in the palace. Xuansu came to the gate and remonstrated sharply.

sentences.zh: 太子出其鼓，對玄素毀之。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent brought out his drums and smashed them before Xuansu.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince brought out his drums and smashed them in front of Xuansu.

sentences.zh: 太子久不出見官屬，玄素諫曰：「朝廷選俊賢以輔至德，今動經時月，不見宮臣，將何以裨益萬一！

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent long did not come out to see his palace officials. Xuansu remonstrated, saying: "The court selected outstanding talent to assist supreme virtue. Now months pass without seeing the palace ministers. How can there be the slightest benefit!
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince had long refused to see his palace officials. Xuansu remonstrated: "The court chose outstanding men to assist your supreme virtue. Months pass without your seeing your palace ministers. How can they help you in the least!

sentences.zh: 且宮中唯有婦人，不知有能如樊姬者乎？」

translations.literal: Moreover, in the palace there are only women. Is there no one with ability like Lady Fan Ji?"
translations.idiomatic: And in the palace there are only women. Is there no one with the ability of Lady Fan Ji?"

sentences.zh: 太子不聽。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince would not listen.

sentences.zh: 玄素少為刑部令史，上嘗對朝臣問之曰：「卿在隋何官？」

translations.literal: Xuansu in his youth was a clerk in the Ministry of Justice. The emperor once asked him before the court officials: "What office did you hold under Sui?"
translations.idiomatic: Xuansu had begun as a clerk in the Ministry of Justice. The emperor once asked him before the court: "What office did you hold under the Sui?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「縣尉。」

translations.literal: He replied: "County assistant magistrate."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "County assistant magistrate."

sentences.zh: 又問：「未為尉時何官？」

translations.literal: He asked again: "Before you were assistant magistrate, what office did you hold?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked again: "Before that, what office did you hold?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「流外。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Outside the regular ranks."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Outside the regular ranks."

sentences.zh: 又問：「何曹？」

translations.literal: He asked again: "In which bureau?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked again: "Which bureau was that?"

sentences.zh: 玄素恥之，出閣殆不能步，色如死灰。

translations.literal: Xuan Su was shamed by this; leaving the hall he could barely walk, his face like ashes of the dead.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan Su was mortified; leaving the hall he could barely walk, his face ashen.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫褚遂良上疏，以為：「君能禮其臣，乃能盡其力。

translations.literal: Remonstrance and Counsel Grandee Chu Suiliang submitted a memorial, stating: "When a ruler can treat his ministers with courtesy, only then can he exhaust their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance and Counsel Grandee Chu Suiliang memorialized: "When a ruler treats his ministers with courtesy, only then can he draw out their full loyalty.

sentences.zh: 玄素雖出寒微，陛下重其才，擢至三品，翼贊皇儲，豈可復對群臣窮其門戶！

translations.literal: Though Xuan Su came from humble origins, Your Majesty valued his talent and promoted him to the third rank to assist the crown prince—how can you again before the assembled ministers probe into the lowliness of his household!
translations.idiomatic: Though Xuan Su came from humble origins, Your Majesty valued his talent, raised him to the third rank, and set him to assist the crown prince—how can you again before the whole court probe the lowliness of his origins!

sentences.zh: 棄宿昔之恩，成一朝之恥，使之鬱結於懷，何以責其伏節死義乎！」

translations.literal: Casting aside long-standing grace and inflicting the shame of a single morning—when he broods in his breast, how can you demand that he lay down his life in loyal sacrifice!"
translations.idiomatic: You cast aside long-standing favor and inflicted the shame of a single morning—when he broods in his heart, how can you demand that he die for you in loyal sacrifice!"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕亦悔此問，卿疏深會我心。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I too regret this question; your memorial deeply accords with my heart."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I too regret this question; your memorial speaks exactly to my heart."

sentences.zh: 遂良，亮之子也。

translations.literal: Suiliang was the son of Chu Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang was the son of Chu Liang.

sentences.zh: 孫伏伽與玄素在隋皆為令史，伏伽或於廣坐自陳往事，一無所隱。

translations.literal: Sun Fuga and Xuan Su were both clerks in the Sui; Fuga sometimes in a great assembly would himself recount his past affairs, concealing nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fuga and Xuan Su had both been clerks under the Sui. Fuga would sometimes recount his past openly in a great assembly, concealing nothing.

sentences.zh: 戴州刺史賈崇以所部有犯十惡者，御史劾之。

translations.literal: Daizhou Prefect Jia Chong, because someone in his jurisdiction had committed one of the ten abominations, was impeached by the censor.
translations.idiomatic: Daizhou Prefect Jia Chong was impeached by the censor because someone in his jurisdiction had committed one of the ten abominations.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「昔唐、虞大聖，貴為天子，不能化其子；

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Formerly, the great sages Yao and Shun, exalted as Sons of Heaven, could not transform their own sons;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The great sages Yao and Shun, though exalted as Sons of Heaven, could not reform their own sons;

sentences.zh: 況崇為刺史，獨能使其民比屋為善乎！

translations.literal: how much more when Chong is only a prefect—can he alone make every household under him virtuous!
translations.idiomatic: how can Chong, as a mere prefect, make every household under him virtuous!

sentences.zh: 若坐是貶黜，則州縣互相掩蔽，縱捨罪人。

translations.literal: If for this he is demoted and dismissed, then prefectures and counties will cover up for one another and release the guilty.
translations.idiomatic: If he is punished for this, prefectures and counties will cover up for one another and let the guilty go free.

sentences.zh: 自今諸州有犯十惡者，勿劾刺史，但令明加糾察，如法施罪，庶以肅清奸惡耳。」

translations.literal: From now on, wherever a prefecture has someone who commits the ten abominations, do not impeach the prefect; only order him to investigate clearly and punish according to law—thus we may hope to purge wickedness."
translations.idiomatic: From now on, when any prefecture has a case of the ten abominations, do not impeach the prefect; only require him to investigate clearly and punish according to law, so that wickedness may be purged."

sentences.zh: 上自臨治兵，以部陳不整，命大將軍張士貴杖中郎將等；

translations.literal: The emperor personally oversaw drilling the troops; because the ranks were not in order, he ordered Great General Zhang Shigui to beat the palace guardsmen and others with the staff;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally oversaw a military drill. Because the ranks were disorderly, he ordered Great General Zhang Shigui to beat the palace guardsmen with the staff;

sentences.zh: 怒其杖輕，下士貴吏。

translations.literal: angry that the beating was too light, he sent Shigui down to the officials for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: angry that the beating was too light, he had Shigui handed over to the officials for punishment.

sentences.zh: 魏徵諫曰：「將軍之職，為國爪牙；

translations.literal: Wei Zheng remonstrated, saying: "The office of general is the fangs and claws of the state;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng remonstrated: "A general is the fangs and claws of the state;

sentences.zh: 使之執杖，已非後法，況以杖輕下吏乎！」

translations.literal: to make him wield the staff is already not according to later practice—how much more to send him down to the officials because the beating was light!"
translations.idiomatic: to make him wield the staff is already improper—how much more to punish him because the beating was too light!"

sentences.zh: 上亟釋之。

translations.literal: The emperor quickly released him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor quickly released him.

sentences.zh: 言事者多請上親覽表奏，以防壅蔽。

translations.literal: Many who spoke on affairs requested that the emperor personally review memorials and reports to guard against obstruction and concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Many memorialists asked the emperor to read memorials personally, lest officials block and conceal them.

sentences.zh: 上以問魏徵，對曰：「斯人不知大體，必使陛下一一親之，豈惟朝堂，州縣之事亦當親之矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked Wei Zheng about this. He replied: "These men do not understand the larger principle. If Your Majesty must personally review each one, it will not stop at the court hall—affairs of prefectures and counties must also be reviewed personally."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Wei Zheng. He replied: "These men do not grasp the larger principle. If Your Majesty must read each memorial yourself, you will not stop at the court—affairs of every prefecture and county would have to be read personally as well."
